The Independent's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn commission. Why trust us?
Andy Burnham vows to crack down on fake discounts, but it might come too late for Black Friday
Misleading “was” prices could soon be banned, but not before the biggest sales event of the year
- Bookmark
“Save 40 per cent on a 65in TV”, screams a certain rainforest-named ecommerce giant. “Half-price electric toothbrush”, shouts another.
Enticing though they might be, those enormous savings aren’t always quite what they seem. That TV you’ve been eyeing up might rarely, if ever, sells for the RRP the discount is calculated from. And that supposedly half-price electric toothbrush might have spent most of the year at the same price.
Fake discounts are littered throughout the web and up and down the high street, but they could soon become a thing of the past. Prime minister Andy Burnham has vowed to crack down on misleading prices as part of a new package of measures designed to tackle “rip-off” business practices.
Under the plans, retailers could be explicitly banned from making misleading claims about how much money shoppers are actually saving. The government specifically highlighted the dodgy practice of artificially increasing the price of a product, only to slash it shortly afterwards, advertising the difference as a saving and giving shoppers the impression they’re getting a better deal than they really are.
The government also wants to target products advertised at a discount despite selling for the same price before the supposed sale, as well as fake “was” prices and misleading RRPs that are used to make a saving appear bigger than it really is.
“We’re putting an end to phoney bargains,” Burnham said. “If something is advertised as half price, it should actually be half price.”
Under the proposals, misleading discount practices could be added to the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act (DMCCA), making it easier for regulators to take action against retailers who use deceptive pricing tactics.
There is plenty of evidence of just how misleading these discounts can be. In 2025, Which? analysed the pricing history of 1,617 TVs advertised with a “was” and “now” price at four major tech retailers. It found that in more than half of cases, the advertised “was” price wasn’t even the price charged immediately before the promotion.
One particularly egregious example was a 65in LG TV sold by Very for £1,499, against a “was” price of £2,499, suggesting a whopping £1,000 saving. Except the TV hadn’t actually cost £2,499 for five months and had been sold at seven different prices since, all of them cheaper than that supposed “was” price.
The consumer group also investigated the prices of 21 electric toothbrushes sold through Oral-B’s online shop in June 2026, and couldn’t find 10 selling anywhere online at their claimed RRP. One Oral-B iO5 duo pack was advertised by both Boots and Oral-B with an RRP of £450 and a claimed saving of £305, despite Which? finding that it was never actually sold online at that RRP by either retailer during its two-month investigation. Historical pricing data also showed it hadn’t been sold at that price on the Boots website since August 2025.
Sports Direct has also come under scrutiny. Which? investigated 160 products sold on its website in 2025 and found 58 where it couldn’t see another online retailer selling the product at or above Sports Direct’s reference price.
But while Burnham might want to put an end to phoney bargains, the crackdown may not actually arrive in time for the biggest discounting event of the year. Black Friday, which sees hundreds of retailers slash prices on thousands of products, takes place on 27 November.
The government says it will launch a consultation on the proposals this autumn, but it hasn’t yet said exactly when the consultation will begin, how long it will last or, crucially, when any new rules might actually come into force. Most consultations last between 8 and 12 weeks.
The government would then need to consider the responses and decide how to proceed before the changes could come into effect.
While the days of misleading discounts are numbered, consumers are going to have to keep their price tracker tools open for a little bit longer. Using an online price tracking tool is one of the best ways to ensure you’re truly getting a good deal.
As well as fake discounts, Burnham also plans to crack down on so-called subscription traps, where customers can find it difficult to cancel a subscription or end up automatically renewing a contract they didn’t intend to sign up for. The government says that new rules around subscription traps will come into effect in January 2027.
For more, we’ve rounded up everything you need to know about Black Friday 2026

The Mossad toured the Fordow nuclear site "many times" in order to understand it, former spy chief Yossi Cohen revealed at the Galilee Conference on Tuesday.

"Its bombing by the Americans is the fulfillment of all my dreams," Cohen added.

Florida woman pretended to have cancer to scam donations out of 200 people, cops say
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:20:17 BST
21:20:17 KST

Florida woman pretended to have cancer to scam donations out of 200 people, cops say
Maribeth Ellen Jones set up GoFundMe page to raise money for treatment she said she needed but used the $40,000 she received to pay off personal debts, police say
- Bookmark
A Florida woman is accused of scamming hundreds of people out of more than $40,000 by falsely claiming to have cancer, according to police.
Maribeth Ellen Jones, 51, set up a GoFundMe page seeking to raise money for the treatment she said she needed, only to spend the donations she received from 238 well-meaning members of her local community in Naples on paying off personal debts, according to the Collier County Sheriff’s Office.
To give credibility to the lie, Jones even had her hair cut short claiming she was getting ready to receive chemotherapy, officers said.
Their investigation into the scam also revealed she had twice previously been the beneficiary of similar schemes on the crowdfunding platform, in which she again lied about having a terminal illness.
Jones, of Bonita Springs, turned herself in at the Naples Jail Center on August 5 after detectives obtained a warrant for her arrest on a second-degree felony charge.
She has been charged with grand theft of between $20,000 and $100,000 and is currently being held at Collier County Jail. Jones is expected to return to court on August 31.
“This is an appalling case because it exploited the kindness and generosity of people who truly wanted to help someone they believed was fighting for her life,” Sheriff Kevin Rambosk said.
“If you lie to steal from the generosity of others in Collier County, we will arrest you and hold you accountable.
“This type of scam not only hurts victims financially, it undermines trust in legitimate fundraisers for people who genuinely need help.”
A spokesperson for GoFundMe told The Independent: “GoFundMe has zero tolerance for the misuse of our platform and anyone who seeks to take advantage of the generosity of others.
“We can confirm fundraisers organized on behalf of Maribeth Jones were removed from our platform, and her account was banned for any future fundraising.
“More than $41,000 was refunded to donors on the platform through GoFundMe’s Giving Guarantee, which offers a full refund in the rare case something isn’t right.”
Kay Ballard, a local resident who donated $100 to Jones’s appeal, told WINK News she felt particularly betrayed because her late husband passed away from cancer.
“I’m really sad she isn’t who I thought she was,” she said.
The sheriff’s office advised the public to do their homework before donating to causes online to ensure their money only goes to verified recipients.
It advised prospective donors to read the comments left by other users, look for regular updates and transparency from the organizer and resist being pressured into giving.

태풍 찬홈 日혼슈 동부 상륙…하네다·나리타 공항 수십편 결항
South Korea
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
21:18:22 KST
21:18:22 KST

진입日기상청 "특이 경로 이동…강풍·폭우·파도 피해 주의"
 
 (도쿄=연합뉴스) 조성미 특파원 = 제15호 태풍 찬홈이 11일 오후 8시께 일본 이바라키현 남부에 상륙했다고 일본 기상청이 발표했다.
 도쿄 북동부인 이바라키현에 태풍이 상륙한 것은 일본에서 관련 통계 작성이 시작된 1951년 이후 처음이다.
 태풍 찬홈은 다음 날인 12일 일본 혼슈를 서쪽으로 관통해 동해로 빠져나갈 것으로 예상된다.
 일본 기상청은 이번 태풍이 보기 드문 경로로 이동함에 따라 도쿄를 포함한 혼슈 동부 간토 지방과 혼슈의 북동부 도호쿠 연안 지역에 강한 바람과 높은 파도에 의한 피해가 생길 수 있다며 주의를 당부했다.
 제15호 태풍 찬홈의 중심 기압은 980hPa(헥토파스칼), 중심 부근 최대 풍속은 초속 25ｍ, 최대 순간 풍속은 초속 35ｍ이다. 
 태풍 중심의 북동쪽 500㎞ 이내와 남서쪽 330㎞ 이내에서는 초속 15ｍ 이상의 강한 바람이 불고 있다.
 이날 오후 4시 30분부터 약 3시간 동안 이바라키현 기타이바라키시에서 최대 순간 풍속 29.3ｍ의 강풍이 관측됐다.
 도쿄 번화가인 오모테산도에서는 태풍 영향으로 보이는 강풍에 가로수가 쓰러지며 주변 통행이 통제되기도 했다.
 
 일본 기상청은 이날부터 다음 날까지 도호쿠에서 서일본 지역에 이르는 넓은 지역에 천둥·번개를 동반한 강한 비가 내릴 것이라고 예보했다.
 12일 저녁 시간대까지 만 하루 동안 내릴 예상 강수량은 간토·고신 지역(수도권인 간토 지방과 서쪽 내륙 지역인 야마나시현·나가노현)이 180㎜, 도호쿠 지역이 150㎜에 달할 것으로 예상됐다.
 일본 기상청은 폭우로 인한 산사태, 저지대 침수, 하천 범람과 낙뢰·돌풍 피해에 주의할 것을 당부했다.
 태풍 찬홈 영향으로 이날 오후 8시 현재 하네다·나리타 공항을 이용하는 항공편 67편이 결항했다.
 JR에 따르면 일본 동부 해안을 달리는 도카이도·도호쿠 신칸센은 오후 6시 현재 정상 운행 중이지만 향후 지연이나 운행 중단이 발생할 가능성이 있다.
 JR 동일본 조반선 이와키역과 미토역 사이 일부 구간 등에서 11일 열차 운행이 일부 중단됐다.
 도쿄 시나가와역과 센다이역을 잇는 특급 히타치 열차는 센다이역과 후쿠시마현 이와키역 구간에서 이날 오후부터 운행이 중단된 상태다.

Qatar sees 'positive' signs in Iran-Oman talks on reopening Hormuz
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
12:17:44 UTC
21:17:44 KST

Doha said Iran and Oman had reached the technical stage of negotiations and were finalising shipping route coordinates, but warned against delay as only six vessels transited Hormuz on Monday compared with 130-140 before the war.
Qatar has seen positive signs in talks between Oman and Iran over reopening the Strait of Hormuz, according to its foreign ministry, despite concerns that demands for compensation could delay an agreement.
“We have heard positive statements from both capitals in the recent couple of days,” Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Dr Majed Al Ansari told reporters in Doha on Tuesday.
“We look to this quite positively, and we are waiting to see what transpires at the end.”
According to Al Ansari, Oman and Iran have indicated that the talks have reached the technical stage, with Tehran saying it was preparing an official announcement.
Oman and Iran have agreed on the coordinates of proposed shipping routes through the Hormuz and are working to finalise an arrangement for vessels using the waterway.
Under the proposed system, ships entering the Gulf would use a northern route through Iranian waters, while departing vessels would use a southern route through Omani waters, according to media reports.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said over the weekend that an agreement with Oman was “very close," yet Tehran has linked a wider reopening of the strait to demands from Washington.
These include an end to US sanctions and military threats, as well as compensation for damage caused during the war.
Compensation not part of current talks, Qatar says
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that Iran should compensate people killed or injured in attacks he blamed on Tehran.
Asked whether Trump’s demand was being discussed, Al Ansari said Qatar was focused on the wording currently being exchanged by Oman and Iran.
“I am not aware of any discussion of compensation within these talks,” he said. “We are not there yet, as we are talking right now about the opening of the strait, diplomacy, the ceasefire and the correct parameters.”
Trump said compensation from Iran should form part of any peace talks, after Tehran demanded payment from the US and Israel for damage caused during the war that began with strikes across Iran on 28 February.
Al Ansari said Qatar was concerned about any delay in reaching an agreement.
“We would like to see freedom of navigation restored immediately in the Strait of Hormuz in accordance with international law,” he said.
Qatar’s priority was to reopen the waterway, maintain the ceasefire and clear the way for wider talks, he added.
Commercial traffic through Hormuz, meanwhile, remains far below pre-war levels.
Only six vessels passed through the strait on Monday, compared with a 10-day daily average of around 11 and between 130 and 140 ships a day before the war, Reuters reported, citing shipping data.
The waterway handled around one-fifth of global oil supplies before the war, while Qatar depends on it to export liquefied natural gas.
Al Ansari said Qatar would support any regionally agreed arrangement that protected navigation and complied with international law.

Everything you can’t do in a heatwave as drought hits most of the UK
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:16:44 BST
21:16:44 KST

Everything you can’t do in a heatwave as drought hits most of the UK
Water companies across the South of England and Wales have imposed hosepipe bans
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
More than half of England and Wales has been plunged into drought as the UK braces for its fifth heatwave of the year.
This week could see highs of 38C in parts of southern England, with temperatures hitting the mid 30s for large areas of the country, as hot and dry weather persists.
Millions of people have restrictions on their water use prohibiting hosepipes, sprinklers, or pressure washers for non-essential domestic tasks to conserve public water.
Some 19 counties across England recorded effectively no rainfall – 1mm or less – during July, Met Office figures show, causing river levels to fall and leaving ground dry and at risk of wildfires.
August has so far seen just five per cent of the expected rainfall for the month, with warnings of more dry weather to come.
As the drought continues to pile pressure onto farming, freight shipping and energy production after the country saw its driest July in 190 years, here The Independent looks at everything this heatwave could stop you from doing.
You can’t use a hosepipe
Nine water companies, including Thames Water, South East Water and Anglian Water, have introduced restrictions on hosepipe use due to the persistent dry weather.
South West Water was the latest water company to impose water restrictions. The utility firm said that due to below average rainfall and a high demand on supplies, customers in Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly, parts of Dorset and Somerset should not use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling up paddling pools.
However, households across the country have been advised to limit their use, with some companies asking customers to pause hosepipe activity where possible, short of a full-on ban.
Filling private swimming pools cold be banned
It’s not just using a hosepipe to water the garden that’s off limits, soon private swimming pools could also face restrictions.
Southern Water has applied to the government for permission to issue a “non-essential use ban” in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.
If granted and put into action, the policy would prevent businesses from activities such as filling private swimming pools.
Car washes could be restricted
More than 70 per cent of England and Wales is in drought and hosepipe bans are in place to help conserve water.
But businesses could also be impacted, including car washes.
In addition to private swimming pools, car wash businesses could also face restrictions from Southern Water.
Excessive exercise outdoors is not recommended
As temperatures are forecast to hit 36C this week experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable, such as older people, babies and young children, should take extra precautions.
That means for many going for a run or a long walk in the midday heat is not recommended.
When the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up, lowering blood pressure and forcing the heart to work harder to pump blood around the body - if blood pressure drops too far, the risk of heart attacks rises.
Sweating also leads to the loss of fluids and salt which can cause dehydration.
Running in hot weather can increase the risk of fainting, heat exhaustion and heatstroke.

Waterway vandalism puts lives at risk and worsens drought impacts
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:15:31 BST
21:15:31 KST

Waterway vandalism puts lives at risk and worsens drought impacts
Environment Agency water control structures suffer repeated vandalism which puts lives at risk and worsens drought impacts. Public urged to report incidents.
The Environment Agency is urging the public to stop tampering with sluices, locks and other water control structures, after a rise in vandalism on its waterways this summer.
The warning comes as drought is declared in Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire.
Damage to water infrastructure is making it harder to manage already low water levels and is putting people at risk.
Tampering lowers water levels, disrupts navigation, harms wildlife and habitats, and creates serious safety hazards.
Ashton Lock, near Oundle, has been one of the worst-hit sites. Vandals damaged its winding wheel, forcing its removal for repair. A temporary fix was fitted, then stolen. The lock’s guillotine gate, which controls water flow, was then tampered with too, draining water needed for wildlife and navigation.
In a separate incident at the same lock, people took a life buoy and its rope from a safety station, used the rope to tie open the lock’s doors, then wound up the guillotine gate, draining water upstream. This has happened repeatedly and has been reported to the police.
Elsewhere, people have tried to break into control panel boxes, climbed on guillotine gates and jumped into locks where there are hidden hazards due to the infrastructure, putting themselves at serious risk.
A common problem on the River Nene is people manually winding up lock paddles which then drain the stretch of river above. The worst-affected stretch is between Upper and Lower Barnwell locks, home to Oundle Marina, where some residents live aboard their boats.
Water levels there drop quickly and, during drought, can take a long time to recover.
People have also been reported climbing onto or breaking into weed-cutting boats left on the riverbank during maintenance.
Ben Thornely, Area Manager for the Environment Agency, said:
  We are disgusted with the level of vandalism we are experiencing at our vital water control structures. This puts lives in danger and has big implications for wildlife and navigation during drought. If you witness vandalism or antisocial behaviour at our assets please report it to the police and to us on 0800 807060.
The Environment Agency is taking action to protect its infrastructure, including placing volunteers at Great Ouse sites to discourage vandals, having CCTV at some locations with some linked to council control rooms with speakers, plus regular and additional safety inspections and more.
Other locations affected include, but are not limited to:
- Northampton Town Lock
- Whiston Lock
- Billing Lock
- Upper and Lower Wellingborough Locks
- Irthlingborough Lock
- Denford Lock
- Nine Arches Mooring
- Lower Barnwell Lock
- Elton Lock *Alwalton Lock
Top tips for river safety:
- 
    Don’t jump or dive in as the depth may vary and there can be unseen hazards.
- 
    Don’t go in near weirs, locks, pipes and sluices. These and some other water features are often linked with strong currents.
- 
    Inland waters can be very cold, no matter how warm the weather. Those going into cold water can get cramp and experience breathing difficulties very quickly.
- 
    Keep a look out for boat traffic. Boaters, especially on larger vessels, can find it very hard to spot swimmers.
More information here: Respect The Water

‘Cursed’ and ‘creepy’ The Cat in the Hat costume goes up for auction
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:15:22 BST
21:15:22 KST

You can now own the creepiest film costume in history
Myers wore the outfit, now ghoulishly empty and cursed-seeming, in the critically panned 2003 children’s movie ‘The Cat in the Hat’
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Ordinarily, if someone says they are dressing up as Mike Myers for Halloween, you might assume it’s a mixup – that they meant to say Michael Myers, the masked killer from the Halloween horror franchise. But what if the former was actually scarier?
This month, the costume worn by the actor Mike Myers in the 2003 children’s film The Cat in the Hat is being put up for auction – but fans have been horrified by the ghoulish look of the empty cat costume.
The outfit – which features huge, empty holes where the eyes should be, giving the costume an eerie, otherworldly vibe – is going on sale as part of a wider entertainment memorabilia auction by Propstore.
Myers’ costume is being sold alongside props such as Frank the Rabbit’s costume from Donnie Darko, the severed toe from the Coen brothers’ The Big Lebowski, and the fax reading “You’re Fired!!” from Back to the Future Part II.
It’s The Cat in the Hat’s furry centrepiece that has got people talking, however, with one social media user describing it as a “cursed item”.
“This is the scariest thing I’ve ever seen in my entire life,” one person remarked, while another another simply wrote: “BURN IT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!”
Adapted from the popular children’s book by Dr Seuss, The Cat in the Hat arrived when Myers was at the height of his powers, hot on the heels of Shrek (2001) and the Austin Powers franchise (1997 to 2002). Dakota Fanning and Spencer Breslin portrayed the two child leads, while Kelly Preston played their mother and Alec Baldwin an ill-tempered neighbour.
At the time of its release, the film was a critical disaster: reviewers had their claws out for the film, which to this day boasts an unusually low score of 10 per cent on the review aggregation website Rotten Tomatoes.
Reaction to the film was so vicious that Audrey Stone Geisel, the widow of Dr Seuss (whose real name was Theodor Geisel), put a moratorium on all further live-action adaptations of the author’s books. Audrey Geisel died in 2018, 27 years after her husband.
The Cat and the Hat’s dubious screen adaptation also preceded a renewed scrutiny of Seuss’s work, with several of his books (not including The Cat in the Hat), now condemned for their racist content.
In recent years, however – fuelled in part by the ageing up of audiences who had been children when The Cat in the Hat first debuted – the Myers film has undergone a soft re-evaluation, with some now regarding it as a cult classic.
A recent TikTok trend has seen users re-edit clips from The Cat in the Hat to adopt a chilling horror aesthetic, juxtaposing images from the film with sinister captions.
Myers spoke about the suit around the time of the film’s release, claiming that the cat costume and makeup was a “piece of cake” after the intense experience of playing the obese Scottish character “Fat Bastard” in the Austin Powers films.
“[That] took about 5 to 6 hours” to get into costume, he said, whereas it took only three to get ready to play the Seuss character.
“And it was very easy to pee in, which is nice,” he added. “That’s how I look at my characters now.”
Which is to say – anyone looking to bid on the outfit in the auction later this month might want to look into a dry cleaner.

The Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, brought the launch event for Spain’s Public Diplomacy Strategy 2026–2028 to a close this Thursday. The presentation of the Strategy marks a milestone in Spain’s foreign action by providing, for the first time, a common strategic framework for the international outreach efforts undertaken by public institutions, the private sector, academia, the cultural sector, sport and civil society.

In an international context characterised by geopolitical competition, rapid technological change and the growing importance of perceptions and narratives in international relations, the Strategy aims to strengthen Spain’s ability to engage in dialogue with societies in other countries, promote its values and interests, and consolidate its global influence.
Launch event

“Spain has long since banned such imports at national level, and the European Union must do the same. Since 2024, there has been an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice which states very clearly that trade in products originating from those settlements is illegal", the minister said on his arrival at the Council meeting in Brussels. “Europe must speak out, and today is a very good opportunity to do so”, he concluded.
Russia’s aggression against Ukraine 
At the Council meeting, ministers also discussed Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine. Ukrainian Minister Adrii Sybiha, who was present at the meeting, reported on the latest developments on the ground and Ukraine’s future needs, particularly in terms of energy ahead of the coming winter. 
Until last year, Russian attacks had resulted in the loss of around 70 per cent of the country’s electricity capacity. To help alleviate this situation, Spain has sent several consignments of electricity generators and high-voltage equipment for electrical substations. Furthermore, Spain is participating in the development of a project involving cogeneration units to ensure heating in the city of Sama.
Donors’ Group for Palestine
Minister Albares also took part this Monday in the second meeting of the Donors’ Group for Palestine, at which he announced Spain’s contribution of 4 million euros in 2026, in addition to the 50 million euros our country pledged at the Group’s first meeting. 
Furthermore, on a bilateral basis, Spain has already contributed a further 5 million euros to Palestine through the AECID’s programmes and the UNDP’s Horizon Fund. 
In 2025, Spain was the fourth-largest contributor to UNRWA, with a contribution of 38 million euros; and in 2026, it has already made contributions totalling 15 million euros. This brings the total announced today to 24 million.
“In the current critical situation, we must take even stronger action to alleviate the humanitarian catastrophe on the ground and stand by the people of Gaza”, said Albares in his speech. “All our efforts must be directed towards moving towards the only political horizon: the implementation of the two-State solution. This is the path to a just and lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis. This is the path to laying solid foundations for regional security and stability”, he concluded.

Albares presents new Strategy for Culture and Sustainable Development in Spanish Cooperation to Council of Ministers
Spain
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
14:12:48 CEST
21:12:48 KST

The Minister for Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, presented the new Strategy for Culture and Sustainable Development in Spanish Cooperation to the Council of Ministers on Tuesday 28 July. This document renews and strengthens Spain’s commitment to defending and promoting cultural rights and cultural diversity as fundamental pillars of sustainable development at a global level.
In the Minister’s words, “this Strategy is based on a clear conviction: without culture, there can be no sustainable development”. Building on this principle, a roadmap has been drawn up to guide Spanish Cooperation’s efforts towards achieving fairer, more inclusive, democratic and sustainable societies.
The Strategy has been drawn up through a broad participatory process involving professionals from Spanish Cooperation and the cultural sector, incorporating contributions from institutional representatives, technical staff, cultural actors and creators. Furthermore, it has been shared with and endorsed by the main coordination and consultation bodies of Spanish Cooperation.
Culture as a right
The Strategy forms part of the new cooperation model promoted by the Law on Cooperation for Sustainable Development and Global Solidarity and the Spanish Cooperation Master Plan, which recognise culture as a human right, a specific area of action and a cross-cutting element of all international cooperation. Accordingly, the document views cooperation as a tool for building bridges, reducing inequalities and expanding opportunities, and regards culture as a human right, a space for participation and dialogue, a driver of social cohesion and a tool for peace-building.
Based on this vision, the overarching objective is to promote the full exercise of cultural rights, fostering cultural expressions in all their diversity to contribute, through culture, to a fairer and more sustainable world.
10 strategic priorities
To achieve this objective, the Strategy is structured around ten strategic priorities. The first four focus on guaranteeing the cultural rights of all people, promoting participation in cultural life, diversity and the fight against inequalities, as well as incorporating a feminist approach, and seeking to strengthen democracy, peace-building and social cohesion.
Strategic priorities 5 and 6 highlight the contribution of culture to economic and social development in Spanish Cooperation’s partner countries by promoting the cultural and creative sector, as well as strengthening the link between culture and education.
For their part, strategic priorities 7, 8 and 9 address some of the key global challenges, such as the protection of cultural heritage, the role of culture in tackling environmental and climate challenges, and the importance of participatory, transparent and democratic communication.
Finally, the last of the strategic priorities is committed to fostering partnerships capable of expanding the scope, innovation and impact of cultural cooperation for sustainable development.
With this new roadmap, Spain calls on institutions, organisations, communities and cultural actors to join forces in defending cultural rights and to move forward, through international cooperation for sustainable development, towards a fairer, more inclusive and sustainable future.

Albares, at the signing of the Gibraltar agreement: “a historic agreement that ushers in a new era three centuries later”
Spain
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
14:12:29 CEST
21:12:29 KST

The Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, attended the signing of the historic agreement between the European Union and the United Kingdom regarding Gibraltar in Brussels this Tuesday. The signing marks the beginning of a new era of coexistence, stability and shared prosperity for the Campo de Gibraltar, Andalusia, Spain and Europe as a whole. The agreement also brings the final outstanding chapter of Brexit to a close and enables Spain to further deepen its bilateral relations with a key European partner and NATO ally, the United Kingdom.
At the Berlaymont building, the headquarters of the European Commission, Commissioner Maros Sefcovic, accompanied by Minister Albares on behalf of the European Union, and the Minister of State for Europe and North America, Stephen Doughty, accompanied by the Chief Minister of Gibraltar, Fabian Picardo, on behalf of the United Kingdom, formalised the agreement with a solemn signing ceremony.
“We have just drawn a line under a long period of discord and opened the door to a new era of coexistence between two communities that used to live with their backs turned on one another and are now joining hands, three centuries later. This is a historic agreement, an agreement for the future, which represents a huge leap forward in terms of stability and prosperity in the lives of 300,000 Andalusians in the Campo de Gibraltar,” the Spanish minister stated after the signing ceremony.
The fence comes down: the last wall in Western Europe
The agreement, which will come into force tomorrow at 00:00, provides for the removal of the fence, thereby eliminating the last wall on the European mainland. It establishes the free movement of people between the Campo de Gibraltar and Gibraltar, which will particularly benefit the nearly 15,000 cross-border workers who commute daily. 
There will be no passport controls between the two territories, and Spain will take over Schengen border controls at Gibraltar’s airport and port. Furthermore, the Spanish authorities will have the final say on the issue and renewal of residence permits.
Collective success
The agreement provides solutions to enable all the inhabitants of a region – hitherto separated by a fence – to live together harmoniously. It eliminates inequalities and distortions, guarantees the free movement of people and goods, safeguards the future of workers and their rights – including unemployment benefits and pensions – and positions the Campo de Gibraltar as a region of progress, opportunity, connectivity and a bright future, something widely sought after by the entire region.
The agreement, Albares asserts, “is a great success, a collective success that marks a new era in the Campo de Gibraltar and opens the area up to a future of prosperity; it closes the final outstanding chapter of Brexit and allows us to further deepen our bilateral relations with a European partner and NATO ally such as the United Kingdom”.
The minister thanked everyone who had contributed to the success of the negotiations leading up to this signing: the mayors of the Campo de Gibraltar, socio-economic stakeholders, the Regional Government of Andalusia and the other institutions, and, most especially, Juan Franco, mayor of La Línea, the municipality that would have suffered the most had an agreement not been reached.
Sefcovic’s Award
Following the signing, the minister presented Commissioner Maros Sefcovic with the Order of Civil Merit, one of the highest honours awarded by our country in recognition of the exceptional services rendered by individuals — whether Spanish or foreign — who have made a significant contribution to the good of Spain. 
With this honour, Albares sought to recognise Sefcovic’s “crucial leadership” in these negotiations, as well as his diplomatic skill and his ability to build bridges, promote European cooperation and strengthen Europe’s position in the world. 
In the minister’s words, “his dedication and commitment have also helped to complete the final missing piece of the Brexit jigsaw: the Agreement on Gibraltar. From the time a political agreement was reached just over a year ago, on 11 June 2025, until today’s signing of the final legal agreement, the work of the Commission teams under your leadership has been extraordinary”.
At the same ceremony, Albares presented awards to other figures who had also participated in the negotiations for the agreement, including the Spaniard Clara Martínez Alberola, senior adviser to Commissioner Sefcovic.
Other meetings
During his stay in Brussels, Albares also met with the High Representative of the European Union, Kaja Kallas, with whom he reviewed the main issues on the international and EU agenda.
He also took part in a discussion with Jeromin Zetterlmeyer, director of the Belgian think tank Bruegel. Under the title End of the old order or a new dawn?, the minister reflected on the many challenges facing European and Spanish foreign policy.

The Minister for Foreign Affairs, the European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, met on Thursday 23 July with members of the Council of Arab Ambassadors resident in Madrid, following concerns raised by Mayor Almeida’s announcement regarding the eviction of Casa Árabe from the premises where it has been based for the past 20 years.

Madrid City Council has been a member of the Governing Council and has always participated in all decisions regarding the administration and management of Casa Árabe that have been taken collectively by that Governing Council. Support for the institution

Casa Árabe is a centre open to the city, whose aim is to bring cultures closer together and promote dialogue and cultural exchange.

Furthermore, students of Arabic at the institution have requested a meeting with representatives from the Spanish MFA to explore ways of ensuring the continuity of their courses and will meet with the Minister next Tuesday.

The Minister took the opportunity to highlight the commendable efficiency with which Casa Árabe’s management team operates, in line with the decisions of the Governing Council to improve its management and administration.
Furthermore, all those present agreed that Casa Árabe is an irreplaceable asset for promoting Spain’s image in the Arab world and an institution that strengthens Spain’s international relations with the countries of the region.
The Spanish MFA reiterates its support for the work of Casa Árabe, an institution dedicated to public diplomacy with the Arab world with a 20-year track record and offices in Madrid and Córdoba, during which time its indispensable role in Spain’s foreign policy has been highlighted; it offers the Madrid City Council a sincere dialogue to reach a solution.
The Spanish MFA points out that the image and international standing of Spain’s capital would be compromised were this decision to be implemented.

Car showrooms
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:11:07 BST
21:11:07 KST

Car showrooms
This publication is intended for Valuation Officers. It may contain links to internal resources that are not available through this version.
This section applies to premises constructed or adapted for use as car showrooms. To qualify as a car showroom for the purposes of this class, there must be a showroom element present at the subject property. Therefore this manual section does not apply to car lots, car supermarkets, garages or workshops or petrol filling stations with some ancillary space.
Primary Description Code: CG3 List description: Car Showroom and premises SCAT code: 042 SCAT suffix: G
3.1 This is a Unit class and each Unit is responsible for the survey and valuation of car showrooms in the class.
3.2 For Reval 2017, it is anticipated that each Unit will have a named individual responsible for the class.
3.3 It is then recommended that each Unit should allocate a named co-ordinator, or Lead Valuer, to act as a point of contact within the Unit. This Lead Valuer will be responsible for assisting in the delivery of the Group’s valuation scheme and also for liaising on value and technical issues with other Lead Valuers across adjoining Units.
The Car Showroom Class Co-ordination Team (CCT) has overall responsibility for the co-ordination of this class. The CCT is responsible for overseeing the approach to car showroom valuations. The team will deliver Practice Notes describing the valuation basis for revaluation and provide advice as necessary during the life of the rating lists. Caseworkers have a responsibility to:
- 
    follow the advice given at all times — Practice Notes are mandatory
- 
    not depart from the guidance given on appeals or maintenance work, without approval from the co-ordination team
The use for planning purposes is usually sui generis.
Car Showrooms should be measured to gross internal area (GIA).
6.1 Internal and external photographs are mandatory and should include photographs of all main areas including show rooms, ancillary offices, parts stores, workshops, mezzanine floors and car wash bays and all rateable plant and machinery.
6.3 Air Conditioning Air-conditioned areas should be identified on the survey, and details of the air conditioning system should also be noted. Air-conditioning to be added as a 5% addition to the appropriate line entry using the air plus adjustment code, the beacon characteristics for air conditioning set to partial if the whole property is not air conditioned.
6.4 Quality Adjustments should not be made for quality other than in exceptional circumstances, for instance where an old workshop is attached to a modern showroom. Generally quality should be reflected in the showroom price.
6.5 Office Area Offices in modern dealerships tend to fall into the following categories
6.5.1 Sales offices and reception areas that face the showroom or are only partitioned from the showroom should be captured as OFF. This will value at a relativity of 100%. These offices are often occupied by sales staff, the dealer principal, etc. The partitioning used is commonly glazed.
6.5.2 Ancillary offices usually form a defined block of offices used for administration, accounts, service administration, human resources and such like. They are often located between the showroom and the workshop. These should be captured as ANO and achieve a relativity of 60%.
6.5.3 All first floor offices should be classed as ANO unless sales areas or reception or where offices are of an exceptional standard when they should classed as OFF. The floor level code should be 01 on the upper floor.
6.5.4 Offices located within the workshop are normally of a more basic quality and these should be captured as OWK which attracts a relativity of 50%. If workshop offices are simply partitioned from the workshop then capture as part of the workshop GIA.
6.6 Allowances to reflect reduced height should ordinarily not be made for accommodation within the main body of the showroom which is below first floor office accommodation, whether the reduced height accommodation is used for showroom or office purposes. Such areas should be included in the normal main showroom or office GIA.
6.7 Land All modern car showrooms have a requirement for land to display cars for sale, customer and service parking and car storage. The land value is a significant item within any car showroom valuation and consistency of valuation method should be adopted across units to achieve consistent valuations.
6.7.1 Although in most cases use by the hypothetical tenant is expected to be the same as actual use of the site, different occupiers can occupy land in different ways. In some cases the land directly in front of the showroom is given over to display but sometimes it can be reserved for customer parking. It is important to have regard to the optimum use of the land if the car showroom was vacant and to let.
6.7.2 Land used for display, customer and service parking should be valued on a price per space. Where car spaces are not marked the measured gross area of the land, less essential access to the workshop only and any landscaped areas, should be used and divided by a notional car space of 20m2. This will reflect circulation. Areas used for vehicle access into the showroom should not be deducted from the area.
6.7.3 Historically, in general terms, the most valuable land was normally at the front of the site however the site layout of modern showrooms may mean that premium sales space can also be located on other parts of the site away from the road frontage. The least valuable land is typically to the rear and usually utilised for car storage or parking areas often for staff. There is usually limited public access to these areas.
6.7.4 Any areas of landscaping (flower beds, embankments etc.) or areas used for essential access into the site or to the workshop areas or petrol filling station or to other separately assessed buildings should be excluded.
6.7.5 Land can be data captured as line entries in the main survey or in Other Additions. The preferred approach is for the display land and car parking to be captured as line entries. In both cases car parking will be expressed as the number of spaces.
6.7.6 Where display and parking land is captured as line entries in the main survey, car parking should be expressed as the number of car spaces and captured using Use Codes VS1, VS2 and VS3. VS1 and VS2 are intended for main display and customer parking areas usually situated at the front and the side of the showroom. As these uses are essentially interchangeable both codes will use the same relativity.
6.7.7 Spaces to the rear of the showroom are normally used for workshop parking and vehicle storage. These areas are not normally accessed by the public. These spaces should be captured as VS3 and will attract a lower relativity to VS1 and VS2.
6.7.8 There display and parking land is captured as an Other Addition, Other Addition Codes VS1- VS9 are available options in the Other Addition tables. Where Other Addition Codes are used, they should ideally be rationalised to VS1-VS3 where possible, to align with the stated line entry method of data capture and valuation.
6.8 Storage Land and Compounds Storage yards if used solely for car storage (no access to the public) can be captured as line entries in the main survey or in Other Additions. In both cases, the land should be expressed in terms of an area per square metre. The use of codes LFH, LFG etc should be adopted.
6.9 Valet Bays located in workshop type buildings should be captured either as WKS or ASO. ASO should only be used where the valet bay is housed in an inferior building to the workshop space.
6.10 Plant and Machinery Details of any items of Plant and machinery present should be noted and identified on the survey in the usual way. Air conditioning see para 6.3. Car washes often have rateable elements such as settings and drainage. Rateable items such as CCTV cameras, fire protection systems, sprinklers, inspection pits and air compressors and receivers and CCTV may also be present. Details of all plant and machinery should be accurately recorded.
6.10.1 For rateability and valuation, reference should be made to the 2017 cost guide.
Rating Surveys should be captured on RSA and plans and surveys stored in EDRM.
8.1 The rental method
The rental method is the appropriate method to be adopted. There is rental evidence available and once adjusted rents can be analysed on a £/m2 basis. The relevant rental adjustment practice note in the Rating Manual, Section 4: Part 1 provides guidance on rental adjustment.
8.2 End allowances
Consideration of end allowances in car showroom valuation should be substantiated by rental or comparable evidence, with reference to relevant case law. For example, allowances for split or multi-franchised sites were rejected by the Upper Tribunal Lands Chamber in Vines Ltd v De Mauny (VO) (2010) UKUT 322 (LC), which addressed a single hereditament comprising two separate car showroom buildings. In this case, the ratepayer’s representative requested several allowances. However, the appeal was dismissed as the tribunal gave precedence to the Valuation Office’s evidence:
  Para 55 — Mr De Mauny (VO) concluded that larger, well-located premises, and those that offered several showrooms linked into shared servicing facilities were more in demand at the Antecedent Valuation Date (AVD) than the traditional, smaller outlets, outweighing any element of discount.
When considering if an allowance is warranted, it is essential to ensure that this does not result in double counting where the main space rate and tone already reflect certain disadvantages, such as poor access or quality, based on comparison with similar showrooms.
If a car showroom is purpose-built for its intended use and developed according to specific occupier requirements, it is reasonable to presume that no allowance for any disability would be warranted, nor agreed between a landlord and tenant. The hereditament must be valued vacant and to let, considering the existing mode or category of use. Allowance requests for showrooms designed to occupier preference should be approached with caution, given their bespoke and purpose built nature.
Valuers should also recognise that building specific allowances for certain disabilities may not require application on adjacent land, such as display or parking areas. Each case should be considered on its own merits.
8.3 Comparison with earlier Rating Lists
Comparing end allowances from previous rating lists may not always be appropriate. Carrying forward such allowances to subsequent lists requires careful scrutiny. In Orkney and Shetland Assessor v Beattie (1988) RA 87, it was noted:
  It is the VO’s duty as part of a revaluation to revalue all hereditaments. The VO does not undertake that exercise by necessarily adopting the same relativities, end allowances…on previous rating lists. The VO undertakes a fresh appraisal of the evidence available and performs a revaluation based on that evidence. Such new evidence can result not only in changes to the general make up of composition of an assessment. It is also an opportunity to establish grounds for new levels of value and new relationships in value between one subject and another. The exercise is evidence led.
In Lamb v Minards (VO) (1974) RA 153, the Lands Tribunal observed that simply carrying forward allowances applied in one rating list to subsequent lists would misunderstand the requirements for revaluations.
  Considering the hereditament vacant and to let, with the tenant fresh to the scheme, the notion that the hypothetical parties would consider end allowances agreed or adopted in previous rating lists when negotiating the rent of the hereditament is plainly wrong and misconceived.
8.4 Burden of proof
The case of Vines Ltd v De Mauny (VO) (2010) UKUT 322 (LC) also addressed the burden of proof. Para 45 of the decision stated:
  It is, however, important to bear in mind that this is an appeal by the ratepayer, not the VO. The onus, therefore, is on the ratepayer to show that the base rate of £160 per m2 is too high, not on the VO to prove the opposite.
8.5 Rental adjustment and analysis regarding fit out costs
It is necessary to clearly identify the basis upon which rents have been determined to be able to apply the correct adjustment to bring them in line with the statutory definition of rateable value. When adjusting rental evidence, valuers should always consider whether fit out additions or costs are required to be reflected via additions to a shell headline rent.
It is common for car showrooms to be let on a shell rent basis, whereby the incoming tenant assumes responsibility for fitting out costs. The hereditament to be valued is a fitted car showroom, so merely analysing a shell rent to determine value for a finished showroom would be inappropriate. Essentially, a fitted showroom commands a higher value than an unfitted shell, with the principle of reflecting fit out costs in rental adjustment confirmed in several court decisions, including Edma (Jewellers) Ltd v Moore (VO) (1975) RA 343 (LT), Hitchings (VO) v Shoosmiths LLP & The Mando Group 2025 UKUT 224(LC) and Bunyan (VO) v Acenden Ltd [2023] UKUT 17 (LC).
Typically, fit out costs must be obtained for new car showrooms let on a shell basis. This requirement also applies when converting a hereditament from previous use such as retail warehouse or department store, or when significant improvements are made to an existing car showroom. Careful consideration must be given to the terms of the headline rent and subsequent cost information, as appropriate. The Valuation Office Built Environment and Minerals team can assist with identifying and analysing fit out data, including provision of Form of Return VO6065.
The recommended approach to analysing rateable items or improvements from costing information is to amortise these costs to lease end or any break clause, using a percentage derived from market evidence. Care should be taken if rent free periods or landlord capital contributions are present. If market evidence is unavailable, a standard decapitalisation rate should be adopted. Once relevant fit out costs are amortised, the resultant figure should be added to the headline shell rent. Rental analysis can then proceed, with the adjusted rent reflecting the value of a fully fitted car showroom.
9.1 All valuations for the 2017 Rating List should be made using the Rating Support Application (RSA).

1. Market Appraisal
1.1 Leading up to March 2024 new UK car registrations experienced a twentieth consecutive month of growth. This included the best March figures since 2019, with just under 320,000 new cars registered with a 24 number plate.
1.2 The number of franchised car dealerships stood at 4,577 in 2023, compared with 4,769 in 2021. This continued a trend of main dealers consolidating the number of sites they operate from, but at the same time, maintaining an approach of often larger high specification showrooms. Certain operators have been active in the market looking at a combination of new purpose built sites or moving into existing units be it those with previous car showroom use or an alternative for example industrial. Naturally if the latter, significant fit out costs are often required to convert to a modern car showroom.
1.3 Despite talk of shifts towards online sales, current research suggests many customers still prefer to visit a dealership before purchasing a new car, at times preferring a more personal face to face experience when spending a significant amount of money. Along with new cars, used car sales remain a key component to many successful showrooms with operator focus at times on offering extended warranties and maintenance plans.
1.4 Electrically powered vehicle sales (including electric hybrid) have continued to grow representing 36.2% of overall sales to January 2024, increasing from 34.4% in the same period in the preceding year. The impact on sales of electric vehicles due to the pace of infrastructure roll out, and the current government putting back the ban on building of new internal combustion engine vehicles from 2030 to 2035, is as yet unclear.
2. Changes from the last practice note
2.1 Changes have been made to the market appraisal section.
3. Ratepayer discussions
3.1 No central discussions have taken place. Car showrooms are valued on market evidence.
4. Valuation scheme
4.1 There is no agreed valuation scheme. Car showrooms are valued in accordance with RM Volume 5 Section 205. The location and age and physical characteristics type of showroom are important factors when valuing this type of property. As a class there may be occasions when local rental or settlement evidence is in short supply and it may be necessary for valuers to cast the net further into other towns and cities, and or differing types of car showroom. Naturally such evidence should be given more weight than any generic market reports circulated on the car sales market. Valuers should thoroughly review the available rental evidence to understand the background and degree of arms length of the parties involved in the transaction.
4.2 Prime locations are likely to have access to large populations through the local main road network and the motorway network. Good locations are often on the edges of larger towns and cities and often co-located with other motor trade premises.
4.3 Highly visible sites with good access, adequate customer parking in prime locations are the most desirable along with a suitable area of land for vehicle display or storage.
4.4 The following examples give guidance on the types of showrooms along with a recommended sub location code to adopt where applicable. However, this is not an exhaustive or definitive list and some flexibility may be required when categorising or comparing sites.
4.5 Notwithstanding the types below, careful consideration is required when reviewing comparable showrooms and evidence. It is not uncommon for older or converted car showrooms to undertake significant refurbishments to bring them into line with the best and most modern sites. Naturally these will often increase the rental value of such sites compared with their previous state, and valuers should seek cost information where appropriate to better inform their valuation decisions post refurbishment.
Type 1: Prime — recommended sub location code: CAR1
These are modern purpose-built showrooms usually built or significantly refurbished since 2010. They are often purposely adapted for the end user and will be to a tightly controlled manufacturer’s design brief. The design standards adopted will often be pan-European or across Europe and North America. They will usually be in the best locations, for example prominent main road sites, close to motorway junctions or co-located on motor retail parks.
They are usually double-height glass walled showrooms fitted out to a very high standard with a distinctive corporate style. They aim to provide a very high-quality retail experience which reinforces brand values. They will have plentiful parking, display spaces and good access. In some instances, and due to restricted or high value land sites or depending on the proximity of the site in question, certain sites will have additional upper floor showroom areas.
Type 2: modern main dealer — recommended sub location code: CAR2
These will be purpose-built showrooms constructed from around 1990 onwards. These will be less highly specified than CAR1 and occupiers are more likely to be the mainstream marques. They may be single storey height or double storey glass walled showrooms. They will be in a wide variety of locations — some will occupy the same type of sites as CAR1 but others will be on main A-road locations historically associated with car sales.
Type 3: older purpose built or conversions — recommended sub location code: CAR3
These will generally be built prior to 1990. They may be purpose built but to designs that now appear dated with lower single storey showrooms with some solid walls and glazed display, rather than fully glazed walls as CAR1 or CAR2. They will tend to be either stand alone or along A-roads in the traditional ‘car-alleys’. In major cities some showrooms may be in converted shops with little or no outside space.
4.5 The Valuation Office transport class coordination team provides the above advice in respect of car showrooms. This is general guidance only and does not replace market evidence and does not take account of any specific local conditions. It will not be unusual for higher levels of value to be applicable in any of the suggested types of car showroom.
4.6 This advice does not apply to car showrooms within central London where showrooms maybe located within a retail pitch and the local retail tone may therefore be more relevant in valuing this type of car showroom.
4.7 In cases where it is correct to value the showroom at a relatively low rate due to the characteristics of the property — for example due to its age or construction — care should be taken in valuing the land used as display and car parking. This is particularly the case where display land and parking are data captured as a line entry. In some cases, the factor applied to the showroom value may produce a value that is too low and does not reflect the correct value of the land — for example where the price/square metre on the land comes level with or below the price/square metre for ancillary storage land with industrial units in the locality. In such circumstances a line adjustment should be carried out so that the land can be valued correctly. This should be done by using a quality line adjustment overwritten to say ‘Land Value’ so that the reason for the line adjustment is recognised as valuation issue rather than an issue with the quality of the land.
1. Market appraisal
1.1 Official Statistics show that since a peak in 2016, UK car sales for both new and used vehicles have fallen. Post Covid, production started to recover in 2021 but widely reported component supply issues has continued to limit output of new cars. This together with similar problems reported as affecting manufacturers in the EU and elsewhere, has contributed to an increase in second-hand car values and sales in 2021.
1.2 Media reports indicate that electric vehicle sales have risen, albeit from a very low base at the previous antecedent valuation date.
1.3 Although media reports suggest there is a trend for manufacturers with the largest numbers of dealerships to downsize, access to a local dealership is still seen as an important part of the sales process in the shift to omnichannel commerce. Such reports suggest that the industry is continuing to move towards larger higher specification properties. The prestige marques frequently seek to have their high value approved used cars under cover, thus increasing the requirement for larger showrooms.
1.4 As at the AVD of 1st April 2021 Covid was in existence. It was anticipated that the vaccine rollout which commenced in December 2020 would reduce its impact on society.

1. Market Appraisal 2008-2015
1.0 Between 2003 and 2007 the market for new cars in the UK saw continued year on year growth with 2,404,000 new car registrations in March 2007. In the year to March 2008 sales slipped slightly to 2,398,000 sales. There followed a gradual downturn over the summer of 2008 with a severe fall in September 2008.
1.1 This prompted the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) to state that the “most difficult economic conditions the industry has faced in 17 years” and called for Government action. There then followed further significant falls in October and November 2008, with November down 36.8% year on year.
1.2 In response to the desperate state of the car retail market the Government introduced the car scrappage scheme on 18 May 2009. The scrappage scheme arrested the slowdown and the market started to recover from the weak performance of 2008 by Autumn 2009. However, 2009 total sales were only 1.99 million, 2010 sales were 2.03 million and 2011 were 1.9 million — half a million sales down on the 2007 figures.
1.3 At the Antecedent Valuation Date of 1 April 2015 annual sales of new cars had seen 37 months of consecutive growth to show 2,476,435 registered in the year to March 2015.
1.4 The SMMT Chief Executive Mike Hawes stated that March 2015 was “The best month this century for new car registrations”.
1.5 At the AVD the new car market surpassed pre-recession levels of sales, but the SMMT predict that the market will level off in 2015.
1.6 Articles in MotorTrader.com (November 2013) and the Vehicle Dealership Property Market Update (2014) carried out by Barber Wadlow considered whether market improvement was reflected in the rental value of car showrooms.
1.7 Both reports refer to improving market conditions. Barber Wadlow reported rental growth on Prime rents inside the m25 suggesting that rents have nearly recovered to their 2007 highpoint. However, it went on to say that outside the m25 prime rents are static and remain below the 2007 levels.
1.8 The Motortrader report states that the market is performing better than one year ago (report dated November 2013). It quotes Rapleys as saying that prime values, on facilities representing key brands such as Mercedes, Audi and BMW, being comparable to that achieved at the height of the market. Conversely, secondary brands are unable to compete at the prime values of 2008. GVA Grimley are quoted as saying that secondary properties are still approximately 25% below the market peak. A further report in March 2015 quoted Colliers as saying that “Values of prime sites in major conurbations are now consistent with the pre-downturn although secondary locations, smaller provincial sites have still some way to go”.
1.9 Both reports refer to a two-tier market with secondary properties taking longer to recover their value. There appears to be stronger growth in the South East relative to the rest of the country.
1.10 Further reports from Motor Trader.com (Oct 2014) highlight rising confidence from investors in dealerships occupied by premium brands, namely, BMW, Jaguar, Land Rover, Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, Audi and Honda. These marques also had requirements for new or upgraded facilities. As the market improves manufacturers will put pressure on dealers to either upgrade older showrooms or move to new, purpose built showrooms. Dealers are under pressure to locate to larger higher specification properties as manufacturer’s ranges grow. Manufacturer owned dealer group subsidiaries such as VW, Honda, Volvo, Kia, Ford and Peugeot are active in developing their retail network and demand high quality showrooms which conform to a strong corporate identity.
2. Changes From Last Practice Note
2.1 The main change from the previous practice note is that car display/parking spaces captured either as VS1 or VS2 as survey line entries are to be valued at a factor of 1.75 times the showroom main space price per m2. Formerly, VS1 was at a factor of 3 x the showroom price/m2 and VS2 was at a factor of 1.5.The adoption of the same factor for both VS1 and VS2 spaces reflects the interchangeable nature of their use between prime display, secondary display and customer parking areas. The factor for VS3 car spaces, where captured as a line entry, remains unchanged at 0.8 of the showroom price/m2.
2.2 Where car spaces are data captured as VS1, VS2 or VS3 in ‘other additions’, the above factors do not necessarily apply and will be subject to a local valuation approach.
3. Ratepayer Discussions
None.
4. Valuation Scheme
4.1 There is no agreed valuation scheme. Car showrooms are valued in accordance with Rating Manual section 6 part 3 — section 205. The location and type of showroom are important factors when valuing this type of property. Notwithstanding the earlier market appraisal from 2008-2015, clearly more weight should be given to rental evidence over generic market reports. If there is a lack of comparable local rental evidence then it may be necessary to cast the net further into other towns and cities, and or differing types of car showroom.
4.2 Prime locations are likely to provide access to large populations through the local main roads and motorway network. Good locations are often on the edges of larger towns and cities and often located adjoining other showroom premises.
4.3 Highly visible sites with good access, adequate customer parking in prime locations are the most desirable.
4.4 The following examples give guidance to the types of showrooms, but this is not an exhaustive list and a wide variety of showroom types exist.
Type 1: Prime
These are modern purpose built showrooms built since 2000. They are purpose-built or purpose adapted for the end user and will be to a tightly controlled manufacturer’s design brief. The design standards will often be pan-European or in the case of BMW across Europe and North America. They will usually be in the best locations, e.g. prominent main road sites close to motorway junctions or co-located on motor retail parks. Some may be on fully re-developed existing car showroom sites. They are usually double height glass walled showrooms fitted out to a very high standard with a distinctive corporate style. They aim to provide a very high quality retail experience which reinforces brand values. They will have plentiful parking and display and good access. The expected marques are BMW, Audi, Mercedes, Jaguar, Land Rover, Lexus. Redeveloped showrooms on cramped sites may have multi-storey parking and occasionally first floor showrooms.
Type 2: Modern Main Dealer
These will be purpose built showrooms constructed from the mid-1980’s onwards. These will be less highly specified than type 1 and occupiers are more likely to be the main stream marques, e.g. Ford, VW, Vauxhall, Skoda, Seat, Toyota, Nissan etc. They may be single storey height or double storey glass walled showrooms. They will be in a wide variety of locations, some will occupy the same type of sites as Type 1 but others will be on main A-road locations historically associated with car sales.
Type 3: Older purpose built / conversions
These will be built prior to 1980. They may be purpose built but to designs that now look dated with lower single storey showrooms with some solid walls and glazed display, rather than three glazed walls as type 1 and 2. They will tend to be either stand alone or along A-roads in the traditional ‘car-alleys’. In major cities some showrooms may be in converted shops with little or no outside space.
4.7 In cases where it is correct to value the showroom at a relatively low rate due to the characteristics of the property for example due to its age or construction, care should be taken in valuing the land used as display and car parking. This is particularly the case where display land and parking is data captured as a line entry. In some cases the factor applied to the showroom value may produce a value that is too low and does not reflect the correct value of the land for example where the price/m2 on the land comes level with or below the price/m2 for ancillary storage land with industrial units in the locality.

Farmer accidentally kills 25 acres of crops after trusting AI advice
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:10:52 BST
21:10:52 KST

Farmer accidentally kills 25 acres of crops after trusting AI advice
AI chatbot suggested a treatment plan that completely destroyed sesame seedlings
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
A farmer in China claims to have lost 25 acres of crops “overnight” after following pesticide advice from an AI assistant.
The 67-year-old from Chuzhou in Anhui province had been using artificial intelligence software for a year prior to the incident, according to local reports, using it to ask for advice on everything from scheduling to fertilising.
Initial success led to him trusting the AI and blindly following its instructions without confirming the information with other sources.
After asking about the best course of treatment for controlling weeds and pests on sesame crops, the AI suggested a treatment plan that completely destroyed a large field of seedlings.
Agricultural experts attributed the error to a herbicide called flufenacet, which can be harmful to sesame fields if not used in a highly targeted manner.
“The seedlings were no good the day after I sprayed them,” the farmer told Taiwanese news site CTWANT.
“The weeds and seedlings died together, and the seedlings died even faster.”
The unnamed AI app that the farmer used reportedly carried a warning at the top of the dialogue page that stated: “AI generation may be incorrect, please verify.”
Similar disclaimers can be found on popular AI apps like OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini, though some users have suffered for not double checking answers provided by chatbots.
Last year, a ChatGPT user developed a rare condition after using it for health and dietary information.
In an effort to remove table salt from his diet, the 60-year-old man replaced it with sodium bromide on the advice of the AI assistant.
After three months of using the chemical in his food, the man developed bromism, or bromide toxicity, and was admitted to hospital to be treated for psychosis – a common symptom of the syndrome.
An article published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which detailed the case, warned that artificial intelligence “can potentially contribute to the development of preventable adverse health outcomes.”
The authors added that AI apps could “generate scientific inaccuracies, lack the ability to critically discuss results, and ultimately fuel the spread of misinformation.”
OpenAI has since rolled out an upgrade for ChatGPT that provides better answers for health-related questions, though the company warned that its chatbot is “not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition.”

When MAGA met FIFA: Inside Trump’s cosy relationship with Gianni Infantino
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
13:10:16 BST
21:10:16 KST

When MAGA met FIFA: Inside Trump’s cosy relationship with Gianni Infantino
President Trump has given his full backing to embattled Infantino as the FIFA president faces ongoing pressure to step down
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
President Donald Trump has thrown his weight behind embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino as the football chief faces ongoing pressure to resign.
The U.S. president warned FIFA that it would be a “terrible mistake” to even consider ousting Infantino, amid widespread backlash over the latter’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.
“He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!”
Swiss-born Infantino has been criticized by a slew of organizations and world leaders, including UEFA, Europe’s football governing body, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
Below we look at the history of Infantino and Trump’s relationship as the pair continue to support each other on the world’s stage.
Red cards at the White House
Trump and Infantino’s relationship can be traced back to 2018, two years after both he and Infantino won their first presidencies.
The commander-in-chief hosted the FIFA president at the White House after the U.S. won the right to co-host the World Cup.
During the meeting, Infantino handed Trump red and yellow penalty cards and joked that the commander-in-chief could use them against the press.
The pair later met again in Davos in 2020, where they dined together.
Infantino was invited by Trump to the White House that same year for the signing of the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between several Middle Eastern countries and Israel.
A closer relationship and a new peace prize
Trump and Infantino appeared to grow closer during Trump’s second term as the 2026 World Cup drew nearer.
Ahead of the world’s biggest football tournament, Trump was handed the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize by Infantino in December 2025.
In a press release detailing the award, FIFA credited Trump for his “pivotal role” in promoting peace between Israel and Palestine.
The award was handed to Trump just months after Venezuelan activist María Corina Machado won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, despite the U.S. president insisting that he was deserving of the accolade.
Earlier this year, Infantino attended a meeting of Trump’s Board of Peace and confirmed that FIFA would build an academy and a 20,000-seat stadium in Gaza.
“We don’t have to just rebuild houses or schools or hospitals or roads,” Infantino said at the event. “We also have to rebuild and build people, emotion, hope and trust. And this is what football, my sport, is about.”
The World Cup kicks off
Once the world’s biggest football tournament began, Infantino and Trump became embroiled in a slew of controversial moments.
During the contest Trump confirmed he had called Infantino personally after U.S. player Folarin Balogun was handed a red card during a match against Bosnia and Herzegovina.
“I said, ‘Gianni, I'd like to make a recommendation: Let the guy in the game,’” Trump said, recalling the phone call. “No, I didn’t say that. I said I’d like to wage a complaint. And actually…I had no idea what was gonna happen.”
Balogun was eventually allowed to play with the U.S. team in a match against Belgium, which ended in a victory for the latter country.
In a statement, Infantino said that the decision to allow Balogun to play was taken by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee and that all of FIFA’s judicial bodies are “independent.”
Infantino also said that he explained to Trump that “there was an ongoing legal process involving FIFA’s independent judicial bodies and that the case would be decided in due course by the competent bodies.”
When the tournament came to a close, Infantino was seen ushering Trump off stage when he awkwardly lingered on stage following Spain’s victory over Argentina in the final.
A White House insider told The New York Post in July that Trump wanted Infantino to become the United Nations’ next secretary general.
The insider claimed that Trump believes Infantino is “respected by everyone around the world” and that he has a “special ability to bring people together.”
Infantino’s World Cup sell off
After the 2026 tournament eneded, Infantino came under fire over a plan to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and other events, with 20 percent of the subsidiary’s shares being offered up to investors.
The plan was dropped after it drew anger and widespread international criticism.
In a scathing open letter, UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation called for an independent review into Infantino’s plan, which they described as a “profound failure of judgement.”
Some countries, including Mexico, Morocco and Argentina, have backed Infantino.
In a statement, FIFA claimed that there were attempts to “undermine” Infantino, who is seeking re-election in March next year.

====================================================================================================

Economic forecasts often miss the mark, yet governments still rely on them
Finland
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
15:10:04 EEST
21:10:04 KST

Economic forecasts are frequently wrong, according to a new report by the Kalevi Sorsa Foundation. Despite this, they continue to play an important role in political decision making.
The social democratic-leaning think tank criticises the close link between economic forecasts and government policy. Its latest report finds that organisations forecasting the development of the Finnish economy rarely get it right.
"Economic forecasts are largely accurate by chance," says Lauri Finér, the foundation's executive director, summarising the report's findings.
Everybody's wrong
The foundation examined GDP growth forecasts produced by seven economic forecasting institutions. The topic is relevant now, as the government prepares to negotiate next year's state budget in September.
Researchers found that all of the forecasters were wrong by roughly the same amount. Even predicting economic growth for the current year is often difficult. According to their report, forecasts made in the autumn for growth in the following year differ from the actual outcome by an average of one percentage point.
"Forecasting institutions are unable to predict economic turning points or even economic growth for the year ahead," Finér says.
According to the report, the Ministry of Finance has generally overestimated economic growth.
Finér says this can lead to unnecessarily large spending cuts.
In addition to the finance ministry's forecasts, the Kalevi Sorsa Foundation examined economic outlooks published between 2016 and 2025 by the Bank of Finland, the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (Etla), Pellervo Economic Research, the Labour Institute for Economic Research (Labore), Nordea and OP Financial Group.
Big differences
The report also argues that the accuracy of economic forecasts is undermined by the theoretical assumptions on which they are based.
Forecasters' models assume that the economy will grow in much the same way as it has in the past. In reality, however, that rarely happens, according to the report.
The group also criticises the opacity of economic forecasting. Economists routinely adjust forecasts using their own expertise and judgement, leaving a personal imprint on the numbers.
"They are, in a sense, adding spices to the pot according to their own taste, but those ingredients are not written into the recipe," Finér says, comparing forecasting with culinary finesses.
To improve accuracy, the researchers call for policymakers to rely less rigidly on economic forecasts and to adjust decisions as new data emerges. They also urge forecasting institutions to make their methods more transparent.
