I bought a wearable air con jacket to survive the UK heatwaves – and it was worth every penny
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
09:17:06 BST
17:17:06 KST

The Independent's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn commission. Why trust us?
I bought a wearable air con jacket to survive the UK heatwaves – and it was worth every penny
I've been eyeing up Japan's famous fan jackets for years – the UK's latest heatwave finally convinced me to buy one
- Bookmark
Forget all other fans. If there's one Japanese invention I've desperately needed in my life, it's a fan jacket. Given we’re all sweating through the ugliest summer in years, I took the plunge and bought one for myself.
First developed in the early 2000s by a former Sony engineer, fan jackets were built to help Japanese construction workers and people working outdoors stay cool. But fan jackets are now a common sight right across the country. Fitted with four battery-powered fans, they continuously circulate air around your body to help you survive hot and humid summers.
With fans and portable air conditioners selling out across the UK, I decided to take matters into my own hands, and bought the Japanese gadget I’ve coveted for years. But could it keep me cool, or did it just make me look like an inflatable Michelin Man, without actually doing anything?
Read more: Best handheld fans, tried and tested
Read more: Best portable air conditioners, reviewed
Fernida fan jacket
- Why we love it 
  - Made my whole body feel cool
 
  - Not too bulky to wear
 
  - Lightweight material
 
  - Machine-washable
- Take note 
  - Poor battery life
 
  - A little noisy
While there are tonnes of brands selling fan jackets in Japan – from Kuchofuku, Makita and BurTle – none of them have yet made it to UK shores. Rather than spending hundreds of pounds importing one across the world, I spotted a replica fan jacket on Amazon and snapped it up. It might be the best decision I’ve ever made.
Made from nylon, Fernida’s fan jacket is a bit like wearing a zip-up windbreaker. There are even two pockets on the side. Nylon’s a great material for a fan jacket because it’s better at trapping the airflow inside your clothing before escaping through the collar and cuffs. It’s also super lightweight to wear (very important given you’ve got four fans stitched into the inside weighing you down).
Two fans sit on either side of your back – one pair of fans at the bottom and one closer to the top. It actually looks pretty cyberpunk from the rear and you can actually see the four fans spinning. But how does it work?
Fernida’s fan jacket comes with a 10,000mAh power bank in the box, which doubles up as the power unit. There’s a cord on the left side that connects the four fans together. Plug that cord into the power bank, turn on the power bank by holding down the power button and watch as the fans kick into gear.
There are four fan speeds that can be cycled through using the power button. Once you’re happy, you can just pop the power bank into the little internal pocket and off you go gallivanting in the sun. You can even ue the power bank to charge your phone or other devices.
But was it worth the purchase? I’m pleased to say that Fernida’s fan jacket is everything I’ve ever wanted. The fans are extremely powerful, blowing around and up your entire body. Because the fans get trapped inside your jacket, it almost creates a funnelling effect. The air escapes through your collar, so it even lifts air upwards, cooling your neck and your face from below.
I’ve been wearing it in 28C weather, and it has been absolutely glorious – both indoors and out. I’d liken the cooling effect to having fans directed at you from all directions. It’s fantastic, and reduces my body temperature by several degrees. I honestly don’t want to take it off.
I’d recommend wearing a sweat-wicking T-shirt or a vest underneath – aka something loose so the airflow can better circulate. The air gets stuck in the jacket that makes it inflate a little bit like a balloon, so you do kind of look like a bulbous Michelin Man. But when it’s this hot outside, who cares?
You can definitely hear the fans running, but surprisingly, it’s not as loud as putting a handheld fan to your face. I’ve got a high tolerance for noisy things though, so your mileage may vary with regards to volume.
It comes in sizes S-XXL, and while you can wash the jacket in the washing machine by taking out the fans, I’d recommend hand-washing it – it’s very fiddly to put it all back in.
There is one major downside to the jacket, and that’s battery life. On the highest setting, the fans only ran for about an hour before running out of battery. On the second fan setting, I was able to eke out roughly 3 hours before it died. That’s pretty useless. And annoyingly, you can’t charge the power bank while plugged into the fans – so you can’t extend the battery life by plugging the power bank into another portable charger.
The power bank itself takes about 2 hours to charge back up. If you’re working outdoors or at a festival, you’re probably going to want it to last a little longer than three hours on a single charge.
Key specifications:
- Fan speed settings: 4
- Battery life: One hour (on the highest setting)
- Sizes: S-XXL
Should you buy the Fernida fan jacket?
If it weren't for the poor battery life, the Fernida fan jacket would be a five-star product. Airflow running over your entire body, up your neck and across your face is so utterly glorious in the summer heat. It kept me so comfortable and it’s undeniably more effective than a handheld fan or a neck fan. It keeps your entire body cool, and it’s just what I’ve needed.
Whether you’re feeling hot indoors or out, I found it to be a fabulous heatwave companion, and I expect many will love it while they’re outdoors gardening, working outdoors or at summer festivals. It’s the most effective portable cooling gadget I've tried so far. But at £72, it’s not cheap and I just wish the battery lasted longer.
How I tested the Fernida fan jacket
I tested the Fernida fan jacket during the UK's summer heatwave in temperatures of around 30C. I wore it both indoors and outdoors while walking and carrying out everyday tasks to assess how effectively it kept me cool, as well as its comfort, noise levels, ease of use and battery life. I also compared the experience with using handheld and neck fans, paying close attention to how well the airflow coped when I was in direct sunlight.
Why you can trust IndyBest reviews
Alex Lee is The Independent’s IndyBest tech editor. Alongside reviewing the latest launches from the likes of Apple and Nintendo, he’s also been reviewing everything to do with cooling your home down and air treatment since 2021. He’s got particular expertise when it comes to cooling devices, having tried and tested everything from Sony’s wearable fan to the best handheld fans. Beyond his experience in real-world testing, Alex is the perfect candidate for this test since he runs warm, making him a harsh critic.

Inbetweeners star James Buckley reveals he’s stopped drinking after being diagnosed with genetic disease
Actor, 38, opened up about changing his lifestyle after being at ‘high risk’ of a heart incident
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
The Inbetweeners star James Buckley has revealed that he’s been forced to give up alcohol and make major lifestyle changes after being diagnosed with a genetic disease.
The actor, 38, opened up about his health on the latest episode of his podcast with co-host and wife Clair, telling listeners that doctors told him that he had a high level of Lipoprotein(a) in his blood – and was therefore at a “high risk” of a cardiovascular incident.
Lipoprotein(a) is a cholesterol-carrying lipoprotein found in blood, the level of which is mostly inherited. High levels of it can increase the chances of heart disease, heart attacks and stroke.
Speaking on At Home With The Buckleys on Sunday (9 August), Buckley – who is best known for playing vulgar teenager Jay on The Inbetweeners, said that he’s been dealing with “health problems” after receiving blood test results.
“I’ve got a genetic disease, mate,” he said. “It’s something to do with my Lipoprotein(a), something to do with that.
“There's nothing you can do about it, by the way. And the doctor's just been like, ’You need to change.’ I'm at a high risk now for a cardiovascular incident. My heart, my arteries. It’s not my fault.”
Buckley added that since receiving the diagnosis, he has given up alcohol and stopped ordering takeaways – with his wife joining him in solidarity.
“I'm not a religious man, but sometimes I feel like there is a God that sort of goes, ‘That’ll teach you,’” he added. “I feel like I've been on this podcast slagging people off that don't drink, and now I’ve been told to try not drinking.
“But I'm going to have a beer soon. I’m just trying to do a little reset, especially after the tour.”
He also admitted that he fears for his kids when they’re older, as he may have passed down the high levels of lipoprotein(a). “Also, another little worry is that because it’s genetic, my children might have it,” he said.
Buckley married former glamour model Clair Meek in 2012, with the couple now parents to sons Harrison, 14, and Jude, 12, who were named after The Beatles’ George Harrison and the song “Hey Jude”.
While Buckley has appeared in comedies White Gold, Zapped and Popstar: Never Stop Never Stopping since finding fame on The Inbetweeners, he’s set to return to the Channel 4 show for a rebooted version on Netflix.
He’ll reportedly be reuniting with co-stars Simon Bird, Joe Thomas and Blake Harrison for the project, helmed by original creators Damon Beesley and Iain Morris.

Chernivtsi backs decision to terminate memoranda with e-scooter operators
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
11:16:30 EEST
17:16:30 KST

The Chernivtsi city council voted on Aug. 10, during a plenary session, to terminate memoranda governing the use of e-scooters in Chernivtsi, according to a YouTube livestream of the session.
The decision was supported by 22 deputies.
The draft decision was initiated by council member Oksana Zubzhytska together with colleagues from the Servant of the People faction.
"Today, Aug. 10, 2026, at a session meeting, we adopted a decision that I initiated together with my Servant of the People colleagues Oleksandr Pikulin and Oleksiy Prosianyi, one we had to fight for over several months. The Chernivtsi city council has supported the draft decision to terminate the memoranda on the use of e-scooters in Chernivtsi!" Zubzhytska wrote on Facebook.
Under the draft decision, the three operators active in the city - Bolt, Vevi and Jet.ua - must clear e-scooters, charging stations and related equipment from community amenity areas within 14 calendar days. If they fail to comply, the vehicles will be moved to a temporary storage lot.
According to Zubzhytska, particular concern was raised by mass use of e-scooters by young children and minors riding on roadways, pedestrian crossings, sidewalks and crowded areas, creating a danger to themselves and other road users. Among the problematic issues, she also cited two or three people riding a single scooter, which raises the risk of accidents, as well as the lack of an effective mechanism holding operators and users accountable in collisions with pedestrians, cyclists or vehicles, compensation for damage, and enforcement of parking and operating rules.
Former Deputy Prime Minister for Reconstruction and Minister for Communities and Territories Development Oleksiy Kuleba earlier told Interfax-Ukraine in an interview that an age limit should be set for the use of e-scooters.
"We submitted such proposals to the Verkhovna Rada committee. Because it's one thing when an adult uses an e-scooter, and quite another when we see how many teenagers are taking up this mode of transport. We can look at statistics on trauma center visits to see the correlation. Unfortunately, the numbers are high," Kuleba said.
He said at the time that certain safety requirements should be established, including on speed.
As previously reported, corresponding proposals for amendments to traffic rules were submitted, providing for the introduction of an age limit that did not previously exist, as well as a number of additional safety requirements, including mandatory helmet use and speed limits.

Lukashenko gathers Cabinet to tackle sensitive budget and social issues
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:16:00 UTC
17:16:00 KST

MINSK, 11 August (BelTA) – Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko has convened a meeting with top officials of the Council of Ministers. The agenda includes several items for which the government has proposed new approaches, BelTA has learned.
 
The first item calls for updating the financing scheme for mineral fertilizer supplies to agricultural organizations. The second concerns changes to the payment of childcare benefits for children up to age three. The third item proposes discussing the feasibility of merging two state bodies – the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection and the State Inspectorate for the Protection of Fauna and Flora.
 
On updating the financing scheme for mineral fertilizer supplies to agricultural organizations 
 
 
 Speaking about the state’s policy in the agricultural sector, the president pledged that support for rural communities would remain in place. The key question, he said, is strict oversight of the mechanisms and volumes involved. “The government draws up monthly schedules for fertilizer purchases by region and identifies funding sources. These include the central and local budgets, agricultural enterprises’ own funds, and loans on preferential terms above all,” the head of state said.
 
 
 
 
 
 The president noted that the overall situation across the country is not bad. “As of 1 August, 92% of the mineral fertilizer quotas had been taken up. Over 90% is a good uptake rate. At the same time, some regions do not fully utilize their quotas throughout the year. For winter sowing, when it comes to nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizers, only half of the regions have achieved full uptake. What is the reason, if there are raw materials available, as you claim, and funding sources have been identified?” Aleksandr Lukashenko asked.
 
 
 
 
 
 In this connection, he drew attention to what is essentially a dead-end situation facing fertilizer producers. Their warehouses are full of unused quota stock, and the expected revenue simply isn’t coming in. “The goods are sitting idle. They were neither consumed by the domestic market nor sold abroad. As I said earlier, in the current situation in the world, enterprises could easily have sold the fertilizers on the foreign market and at a higher price,” the head of state remarked.
 
 
 
 
 
 “For next year, it is proposed to increase fertilizer purchases by another 18% to support the planned growth in agricultural production; that much is clear. Consequently, even more funds will be needed, roughly Br3 billion in total, along with reliable funding sources,” Aleksandr Lukashenko stated. “To lower the cost of mineral fertilizers for farmers and ensure quota uptake, the government has developed new approaches.”
 
 
 
 The Council of Ministers proposes that half be paid for from the central budget, with funds channeled directly to the manufacturers. For the other half, it is proposed to use agricultural organizations’ own funds, bank loans, and local budgets. The manufacturer would make deliveries only after full payment. Oversight of implementation would fall to the chairs of regional executive committees.
 
 
 
 The president pressed for hard numbers and a clear rationale to show exactly how the new scheme would affect the final price of fertilizers for farmers. “What concerns us is the money we are spending and what kind of return we will get from it, not quotas first and foremost. And another thing: will this new approach eliminate the practice of unscheduled appeals to the president for additional resources? Most importantly, will it motivate the average agricultural enterprise director to work more efficiently, given that we are all pitching in to solve his problems?” Aleksandr Lukashenko raised a number of questions. 
 
 
 
 Overhauling state support for families with children 
 
 
 The agenda included discussion of a legal act concerning childcare benefits.
 
 
 
 
 The head of state emphasized that parents in Belarus receive very substantial financial support. There are lump-sum payments at childbirth (around Br5,000 for the first child and more than Br7,000 for the second and subsequent children). There is a family capital program for large families – currently over Br35,000. And there are monthly allowances of at least Br1,000.
 
 
 
 
 “It would seem – just have children! They’ll be fully supported by the state. But the modern world has become too pragmatic. Young people first seek to establish themselves – through education and career – and only afterward consider having children,” the president said.
 
 
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko noted that just 10 years ago, Belarusians’ standard of living was half of what it is today: GDP per capita in 2015 was about $18,000, while in 2025 it was roughly $35,000. “But twice as many children were born back when we were poorer (nearly 120,000 in 2015 versus 55,000 in 2025),” the head of state observed.
 
 
 
 
 “To keep our nation from disappearing and to ensure there’s a workforce to keep the country going, it’s as simple as two plus two: two parents – two children. That’s the baseline, as the young people say. And better yet – three or more,” the president stressed. “Therefore, at the state level, we need to find a workable formula that, first, will reinvigorate demographic trends. Second, it will motivate people toward conscious motherhood and fatherhood and make them a trend. That way, we will preserve and grow our population.”
 
 
 
 
 To address demographic challenges, the government has proposed a radical overhaul of state support for families with children. Before arriving at specific decisions, the president outlined a number of fundamental questions. “Is there a guarantee that expanding financial incentives will actually give a boost to the birth rate?” Aleksandr Lukashenko asked. The head of state also inquired about international experience, the long-term effect (over five years or more) of substantial state support, and its impact on the budget and the country’s economy.
 
 
 
 
 On merging the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection and the State Inspectorate for the Protection of Fauna and Flora  
 
 
 Aleksandr Lukashenko recalled that this topic had come up when the current head of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection was appointed. “In the complex field of environmental protection and control over natural resource use, these agencies work cohesively and seemingly successfully: they uncover criminal schemes and prevent various violations. Poaching, for example, has been reduced to a minimum,” he emphasized.
 
 
 
 
 
 At the same time, as the president noted, apart from poaching, there are other issues in the realm of environmental protection. “This is about protecting our nature, and we need to go all in on this, because it truly is our treasure,” he said. “In the middle of a vast civilization, in Eurasia, lies the cleanest corner of the planet. It is remarkable, really, that we have managed to preserve it.”
 
 “The inspectorate must tackle not only poaching, but also those who have made a habit of polluting. Both the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection and the inspectorate are falling short here. So let’s not act as if we have been blessed with good fortune and can rest easy; there are plenty of problems that need to be addressed,” the head of state emphasized.
 
The president noted that at first glance, there appear to be no obvious obstacles to further combining the efforts of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection and the State Inspectorate for the Protection of Fauna and Flora. “At the same time, I know that the State Secretariat of the Security Council did not support this initiative. We will hear their view,” he added.

Albania's Cheerful 'AI Minister' Is the Product of a Government Agency Under Investigation for Massive Corruption
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:15:00 UTC
17:15:00 KST

Reported by
Last September, Albania made headlines around the world when it introduced the world’s first-ever “AI minister.”
Diella, which means “Sun” in Albanian, was a chatbot that had been promoted to ministerial status. Her remit, Prime Minister Edi Rama announced, was to ensure that “public tenders will be 100 percent free of corruption.”
“I do not have personal ambitions or interests,” the AI avatar, who dresses in traditional costume, told parliament in her maiden speech. “I only have data, a thirst for knowledge, and algorithms dedicated to serving citizens… free from prejudice, discrimination, clientelism, nepotism, or corruption.”
At the time, there were doubts over whether Diella could offer any real solution to Albania’s long-standing corruption problem.
It appears that some of the reservations may have been well-founded. Experts caution that Albania’s plan to use Diella as a buffer against corruption has flaws, given that information generated by AI is not inherently neutral, and that there has been little transparency so far on how the technology will be deployed.
These concerns have been further compounded by an explosive corruption case inside the very agency that created the virtual assistant.
The Albanian AI minister, Diella. (Credit: shteg.org)
According to anti-corruption prosecutors, the leaders of the government agency that developed Diella, the National Agency for the Information Society (AKSHI), are suspected of rigging tenders in favor of a criminal group that profited from privileged access to the agency’s contracts.
The special prosecutors accuse the AKSHI officials (in a court order issued by a judge) of receiving kickbacks that included wine boxes filled with cash. The agency’s director and deputy director were charged in the same document with violating public tender rules and cooperating with a criminal organization.
Two owners of IT firms — one of whom was arrested last month in France, where he was found to also own a castle — have also been charged with organizing and collaborating in the scheme.
The deputy director of Tirana’s police force, meanwhile, has been suspended from duty while under investigation for allegedly covering up or collaborating with the group's illicit activities.
AKSHI, the government, and lawyers for the accused businessmen and officials did not respond to OCCRP’s questions. None of the individuals have been indicted, as the investigation is ongoing.
In total, authorities ordered a seizure of assets — including real estate, vehicles, bank accounts, and cash — worth more than 40 million euros connected to the scheme.
Diella’s development was not one of the tenders involved in the alleged corruption scheme. Yet the allegation that graft ran to the top of the agency which created her has deepened doubts about the government’s plan to use the technology to tackle corruption more broadly.
Albania is under heavy pressure from the European Union to root out corruption in order to proceed with its years-long effort to join the bloc. According to the latest assessment from Brussels, which was released before the AKSHI scandal broke, perceptions of corruption in the public sector remain high.
“Even the most sophisticated AI is only as good as the humans who build, operate, maintain, and improve it,” said Erjon Curraj, an expert in digital transformation at the SCiDEV Center, a Tirana-based think tank, told OCCRP.
“Who feeds the data, and who verifies its integrity? Who catches errors and hallucinations before they become decisions? The people who maintain such a system can nourish it or let it quietly degrade.”
Bojan Perkov, the Digital Policy Coordinator of the SHARE Foundation, a non-profit focused on digital rights and security in the Western Balkans, also warned that cleaning the state of corruption “cannot be achieved with any kind of ‘magic’ technology, and especially not AI tools.”
Flashy announcements about a new use of technology are “often used for politicians' publicity” rather than forming part of a strategic plan to bring “long-term benefits for a society, which should build its governance mechanisms based on rule of law,” he added.
The Albanian government, ASHKI, and the office of the Prime Minister did not respond to requests to comment.
'Cooperating with a Criminal Organization'
In the summer of August 2025, Albanian tech entrepreneur Gerond Meçe walked out of his home in Tirana and was confronted by a black Land Rover Defender with a police siren.
A man in uniform emerged and called his name, Meçe later told authorities. Grainy CCTV images also captured the moment.
"You need to come with us, get in the car," Meçe recalled the man saying, claiming to be an official from Albania’s anti-graft unit, the Special Structure against Corruption and Organized Crime (SPAK).
But as the bulky 4x4 pulled out of the car park and the men put a hood over Meçe’s head, it became clear that this had been a ruse.
"We're asking you to cooperate,” one of the men told Meçe when the car stopped about an hour later, according to testimony he later gave to actual SPAK prosecutors. “Otherwise you'll have a bullet in your head."
Prosecutors suspect the kidnapping was orchestrated by the criminal group that had allegedly been running ASKHI’s kickback scheme, and was aimed at convincing Meçe to withdraw his tech company’s appeals on more than a dozen tenders put out by the agency.
Meçe’s firm had complained that the tenders — which covered a range of projects including making software for state agencies like the police — appeared to be rigged in favour of insiders, a move that had stalled AKSHI’s contracting process with the alleged criminal collaborators.
After Meçe agreed to retract his appeals, the kidnappers let him go.
When reached for comment, SPAK said the investigation was ongoing and that the case had not yet been sent to trial.
Killing the Bribe
Diella was first launched by AKSHI as a chatbot in January 2025 with the goal of helping citizens navigate the e-Albania government web portal, where they could access everything from birth certificates to pensions.
Her rollout was part of the agency’s drive to digitize government services and help speed the country’s accession to the European Union, which Albania hopes to achieve by 2030.
Some tech-savvy Albanians have found the online portal helpful. Klodisa Përnezha, a 26-year-old nurse living in Tirana, said it has made her work faster, more efficient, and better organized.
“I no longer need to wait in lines at institutions or waste time traveling in person for every document,” she said. “Most services are now completed online, from home or even through my phone.”
But with 95 percent of the government’s services now exclusively online, some Albanians are struggling to use Diella’s assistance on their own.
This has led to the emergence of a cottage industry of middlemen who have opened up offices around Tirana to help clients navigate the portal for a fee.
Some see this service as merely an expensive formalization of the old system, in which one customarily slipped the equivalent of $2 to a local administrative clerk to expedite a family certificate or property deed.
"Before, you knew whom to give the [cash] to, and you received the service. Now, you give it without thanks. It’s obligatory,” said Bajram Hasxhepa, a 66-year-old who suffers from diabetes and lost the lower part of his legs 13 years ago.
For Hasxhepa, the "seamless" digital state looks like this: He wheels himself 600 meters down the street to an office supplies shop that doubles as a private internet booth, just to get a family certificate printed.
The shop has no wheelchair ramp, so he is forced to sit outside on the sidewalk, shouting his personal details over the traffic to a young clerk inside — and paying a roughly $12 "application fee" for a document the state says is free.
‘Diella is Pregnant’
Diella’s remit has been steadily growing since she was first unveiled to the public.
From her beginnings as a chatbot for the government’s online portal, she was elevated to the role of cabinet minister in September 2025. Then, a month later, there was more news.
"Diella is pregnant and she’s expecting 83 kids," the prime minister quipped at an international business conference in Berlin in October.
These digital "children," he explained, would participate in parliamentary sessions, analyze EU legislation, and even alert absent politicians if a rival mentions their name, so they can prepare a response.
Diella, who floated like a modern-day genie on a screen above the audience, added her two cents: “Artificial Intelligence will help identify investment barriers before they become crises, detect corruption risks before they become scandals, and predict market opportunities before they are missed.”
For retiree Sadete Suta, who has spent the last year paying middlemen to interact with Diella so she can secure her pension, Rama’s joke didn’t land so well.
“We’ll bring her some pancakes," she said sarcastically, referring to a local tradition of delivering special foods to new mothers.
As part of her ministerial duties, officials promise, Diella will soon be monitoring state purchases, evaluating bids, and overseeing billions of euros in government tenders. The exact details of her role in all this, however, have yet to be spelled out.
Black Box
Experts caution that Albania’s plan to use Diella as a defense against corruption has holes.
“Diella will inevitably sort, prioritise, and frame the information on which political decisions are based,” noted an essay published by the European Union Institute for Security Studies, a foreign and security policy think tank.
“The question is therefore to what extent human judgments are shaped, constrained, or biased by these outputs.”
Furthermore, without clear oversight or traceability of her “decisions,” Diella “risks adding a further layer of opacity to governance rather than reducing it,” the think-tank warned.
Curraj, from the digital transformation from the SCiDEV Center, urged the government to create a transparent "sandbox" — a secure testing environment where the technology could run safely without impacting the real world, and where academics and civil society experts could offer feedback.
Without this step, "you cannot launch it in live production,” he said.
Who exactly will be held accountable for Diella’s decisions — something that the opposition has raised as part of a complaint it filed with the constitutional court— remains unclear.
Responding to critics who argue that algorithms can be manipulated and controlled, Rama said Diella’s decision-making “will remain fully auditable.”
Final decisions will still be made by officials based on the information Diella provides, he said.
“Anyone who wishes to review the process manually will be able to do so. Nothing that emerges from the system will be untraceable.”
But as the public waits for more details, Diella has already run into legal trouble herself.
In April, Anila Bisha, the actress on whom Diella’s likeness and voice are based, filed a lawsuit against the government, accusing it of misusing her image, which the government denies.
Bisha said she gave permission for her image to be used as an AI-powered virtual assistant — but not as a politician in Rama’s government.
The actress discovered the change when watching the news with her husband, and has since faced harassment in the street and online, she told OCCRP.
“There are those who tell me that I have gained fame. But I do not see any fame here, I even say this is not fame at all.”
Now she worries about what Diella might be assigned to do next.
“I have a fear that with the development technology has taken, I no longer know how else they might use my face and my voice,” the actress said. “My data has been put on the market.”

Russia says it struck military-related warehouses and steel works in overnight Ukraine strikes

Ukraine's president has repeatedly sounded the alarm over deepening military ties between Moscow and Pyongyang, often while appealing for more Western air-defence supplies.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Russia fired North Korean missiles in an overnight attack that killed six and wounded 19 in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia.
"The city was struck with North Korean ballistic missiles, Zircons, and guided aerial bombs," he said, referring to Russia's hypersonic cruise missile system, Zircon.
Zelenskyy had warned on Monday evening that Russia was preparing to station more North Korean troops on its territory and had already received more ballistic missiles from Pyongyang.
He has repeatedly sounded the alarm over deepening military ties between Moscow and Pyongyang, often while appealing for more Western air-defence supplies.
"This is the first time they cannot wage war without supplements from North Korea," he said in his nightly address, referring to Russian forces.
"They are now preparing to deploy an additional contingent of Koreans on their territory. They have received, just imagine, additional ballistic missiles from North Korea," he added.
Only certain air defence systems, including US Patriots, are capable of intercepting ballistic missiles.
A shortage of PAC-3 interceptors has worsened since the war launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.
At the same time, Ukraine has been increasing its strikes against Russian cities far from the border.
At the weekend, Zelenskyy said a decision had been taken for 30,000-50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on Russian soil. He did not explain how he obtained those figures.
North Korea has become one of Russia's closest military partners since Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a mutual defence pact in June 2024.
Moscow used the North Korean troops in a counteroffensive later that year that pushed Ukrainian forces out of the border Kursk region.
The overnight Russian attacks spanned Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk, regional authorities said.
Russia's defence ministry said its forces "delivered a group strike with high-precision ground-based weapons, hitting military-industrial enterprises and transport-logistics centres in the cities of Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia."
In Zaporizhzhia, Ivan Fedorov, head of the regional military administration, said Russian forces launched a "massive" attack using missiles and guided aerial bombs.
"Six people were killed and 19 others wounded," Fedorov wrote on Telegram, updating an earlier toll of five dead.
In the eastern Dnipropetrovsk region, Russian drone and artillery strikes on five districts killed three people and wounded five others, regional military administration head Oleksandr Ganzha said on Telegram.
Journalists in Kyiv said they heard a series of explosions shortly after midnight after authorities issued a missile alert.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on social media that the capital was "under ballistic missile attack."
Ukraine's emergency service said a warehouse caught fire and one person was wounded.
Kursk offensive
About 600 North Korean troops were killed fighting for Russia against Ukrainian forces, South Korea’s spy agency told lawmakers last year.
North Korea has suffered some 4,700 casualties, including injuries and deaths, the South Korean National Intelligence Service (NIS) told a parliamentary committee.
About 2,000 injured soldiers were repatriated to North Korea by air or train between January and March, according to the NIS.
The dead soldiers were cremated in Russia before their remains were sent back home, the intelligence agency said.
The assessment came after Pyongyang confirmed for the first time that it had sent troops to help Russia recapture parts of the Kursk region, which Ukraine took control of in a surprise incursion.
Meanwhile, North Korea's economy was showing signs of recovery as Pyongyang deepened trade and diplomatic ties with Russia and China, South Korea's unification ministry said in a report in April.
Rigid socialist planning and high military spending undermined growth in North Korea for years, as have sweeping international sanctions aimed at scuppering its development of nuclear weapons.
China has long been the diplomatically isolated country's main economic backer, though Pyongyang has also drawn closer to Moscow since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Those relationships are now driving an improved economic outlook, with the North appearing to have "moved beyond a period of contraction" and "entered a phase of gradual recovery," according to the South Korean ministry.
Analysts said the North was also receiving economic and military technology assistance from Russia in return for sending troops and ammunition to help it fight Ukraine.

Turkish foreign minister to pay official visit to Libya

17:13:32 KST

Türkiye's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will pay an official visit to Libya on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources.
Fidan will hold meetings in Tripoli and Benghazi as part of his visit, the sources said.
During the talks, Fidan is expected to comprehensively discuss agenda items aimed at strengthening Türkiye-Libya relations based on historic bonds of brotherhood and an understanding of mutual benefit in all areas, particularly political, commercial, energy, military, and defense ties.
Fidan is also expected to exchange views on recent developments in Libya's political process, underline the importance Türkiye attaches to Libya's stability, and note that Ankara is closely following US initiatives and the UN-led political process.
Based on the priority of achieving lasting peace and maintaining calm in Libya, Fidan is expected to hold consultations on Türkiye's potential contributions to steps taken under Libyan ownership and leadership.
As a reflection of Türkiye's approach of making no distinction between Libya's west, east, and south under its "One Libya" policy, Fidan is expected to emphasize Ankara's determination to strengthen its dialogue with Libyan officials.
He is also expected to stress the significance of protecting the two countries' common rights and interests in the Eastern Mediterranean in line with a win-win approach.
Fidan is expected to express Türkiye's desire to further develop existing energy cooperation with Libya on the basis of mutual benefit and implement new projects.
He is also expected to say that the safe and sustainable continuation of the activities of Turkish companies, which have a significant presence in Libya, particularly in the contracting sector, would contribute to advancing and deepening economic and commercial cooperation.
Fidan is also expected to exchange views on regional and global developments, particularly the Palestinian issue and the situation in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
He is expected to emphasize the importance of addressing regional issues through dialogue and diplomacy based on regional ownership and joint efforts, while highlighting the strategic role of military and defense cooperation in this context.
Fidan is also expected to underline the need to strengthen and sustain efforts for lasting peace in Palestine and for the international community to adopt a principled, determined, and unified stance on the issue.
 
Türkiye-Libya ties
Türkiye and Libya share deep-rooted historical, cultural, and people-to-people ties, with bilateral relations being developed in all possible areas on the basis of mutual benefit to contribute to lasting peace, stability, and security in Libya, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources.
In this context, reciprocal high-level visits between the two countries have continued to gain momentum.
Most recently, Libyan Government of National Unity Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibeh was received by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on April 18, on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum.
Under its "One Libya" policy, Türkiye prioritizes preserving Libya's unity, integrity, and cohesion, and continues its active efforts to establish lasting stability and maintain calm in the country, the sources said.
Based on this approach, Türkiye maintains dialogue with all sides in Libya without distinction between the west, east and south, while working together with Libyans to further advance relations in all areas.
Türkiye supports UN efforts to hold credible, fair, and transparent elections in Libya and cooperates with all Libyan stakeholders and the international community. Ankara emphasizes that steps taken as part of political efforts toward a prosperous and united Libya, which the Libyan people deserve, should be carried out under Libyan ownership and leadership, the sources added.
Ankara continues its efforts toward the unification of Libya's military institutions as part of its "One Libya" policy, and the active participation of elements from western and eastern Libya in the EFES 2026 exercise, held on April 11-May 21, is considered "a significant step in this direction," they also said.
Economic relations
Bilateral trade volume between the two countries stood at $3.5 billion in 2025. Despite the current fragile conditions, Libya remains an important market for Türkiye's private sector.
Bilateral economic relations also continue to develop in various areas, particularly the contracting sector. In this context, the 22nd Türkiye-Libya Joint Economic Commission Meeting was held in the Libyan capital Tripoli on Jan. 24.
Türkiye's contracting sector undertook its first overseas project in Libya in 1972. Turkish companies have so far carried out 633 projects worth $31 billion in the country.
Libya ranks fourth among the countries where Turkish companies have undertaken the highest number of projects.
Turkish companies currently have more than 40 ongoing projects in Libya, with a combined value exceeding $2.3 billion.
The steadily developing ties between Türkiye and Libya are also creating new opportunities in the energy sector.
In February, the Turkish Petroleum Corporation won the right to jointly operate two oil fields in Libya's first licensing round in 17 years.
An agreement concerning the fields was signed in Tripoli on June 15.

Ukraine’s 40-day campaign has not brought the war closer to an end
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:13:31 UTC
17:13:31 KST

Ukraine’s 40-day campaign has not brought the war closer to an end
Kyiv is facing a brutal Russian response as its air defence missile stocks dwindle.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s 40-day campaign to “influence” Russia into ending the war expired last week without much fanfare. The campaign involved high-intensity attacks with long-range missiles that were meant to compel Moscow into accepting Ukraine’s terms. But it does not seem to have worked. Russian President Vladimir Putin is still unwilling to make any concessions.
After yet another failed escalation, Kyiv finds itself facing the same unpalatable choice: continue the war and experience catastrophic devastation, or negotiate peace, largely on Putin’s terms.
The Russian president is demonstrating the kind of merciless consistency that has characterised the Russian approach to this conflict since its inception. The longer Ukraine resists, the more damage it suffers. Any attempt at escalation that tangibly hurts Russia results in a response of even higher magnitude.
That’s exactly what happened with Zelenskyy’s campaign. Ukrainian missiles and drones hit Russian oil refineries, precipitating a serious fuel crisis in Russia and an acute one in Russian-occupied Crimea. Lately, Ukrainian forces shifted their emphasis to the logistical hubs of Russia’s online marketplace Wildberries, hoping to undermine a myriad of associated businesses and by extension the banking sector.
These attacks did not bring about the desired results: political unrest and protests against the war. Moscow was able to ease the fuel crisis in recent weeks and enhance air defences at key infrastructure. Wildberries is adapting by moving its logistical hubs to neighbouring Kazakhstan, which is part of the Russia-led customs union.
In response to the Ukrainian “influence campaign”, the Russian army launched brutal strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure, which resulted in the country’s Black Sea ports shutting down. This is having a devastating effect on companies handling Ukraine’s two main export commodities – grain and ore.
Russia also embarked on indiscriminate attacks on logistical hubs belonging to Ukraine’s major retailers, such as Epicentr and Rozetka, resulting in a near-complete loss of business for their politically influential owners. The Russian military also targeted Ukrainian petrol stations and even individual petrol trucks.
Meanwhile, the Russian offensive on the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration in the north of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine is continuing while the Russian army is building what it calls a “security belt” by grabbing pieces of Ukrainian territory along the Russo-Ukrainian border in the north.
The Ukrainian escalation, which was announced just before NATO’s Ankara summit in July, and the accompanying media campaign claiming it was “turning the tide”, were aimed at swaying United States President Donald Trump on Ukraine. In Ankara, it seemed like a success.
However, Trump’s subsequent statements made it clear he has not changed his mind. He even walked back his promise to provide Ukraine with a licence to produce Patriot missiles. A “draconian sanctions” bill aimed at Russia was approved by the US Senate but faces an uncertain future in the House of Representatives. Even if it is voted into law, it is far from certain that it would be able to shift the course of the war in Ukraine’s favour.
Meanwhile, Ukraine is struggling to defend itself. Trump’s war on Iran has largely deprived it of missiles for its Patriot air defence systems, as a result of which almost every Russian missile has reached its target in the latest series of strikes on Kyiv and other cities.
That means Ukraine is in for the harshest winter ever since the start of Russia’s all-out invasion in 2022. Ukrainian officials fear that on top of destroying more energy infrastructure, Russia is going to target sewage and water supply systems, which could render Ukrainian cities unliveable.
With this devastating prospect on the horizon, painful compromises at the negotiation table once again emerge as Ukraine’s only way out of national catastrophe. Despite his defiant rhetoric, Zelenskyy might be moving in that direction.
In the cabinet reshuffle that he undertook in the middle of the 40-day campaign, he sacked Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, the person who spearheaded the mid- and long-range strikes against Russia. The Ukrainian president subsequently withstood pressure to reinstate him from his staunchest Western allies and their Ukrainian proxies who tried to stage a nationwide protest against the move.
In less publicised development, Zelenskyy also fired the deputy prime minister for European integration, Taras Kachka. Months before his dismissal, Kachka – along with European Union Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos – authored a 10-point reform plan to fight corruption and improve the rule of law in Ukraine.
Some of the reforms in that plan would severely limit the president’s ability to control law enforcement, particularly when it comes to anticorruption investigations. The Ukrainian parliament, controlled by Zelenskyy, has been refusing to adopt these laws, not least because they would endanger the president, whose immediate entourage has been the subject of a massive anticorruption probe since last fall.
Risking alienating the EU, which is Ukraine’s main funder, is a dubious proposition in a time of war. But if Zelenskyy decides to sue for peace with Putin, he would need to eliminate the risk of impeachment and maintain a Russian-styled security vertical to prevent any dangerous backlash against what’s bound to be very unsavoury terms of settlement.
He must feel emboldened by the fairly weak societal response to Fedorov’s dismissal – not many Ukrainians were keen to stage revolution for a Western media darling.
But Zelenskyy’s personal risk of being universally proclaimed the scapegoat for the failure to deliver a strategic defeat of Russia remains very high. Opting out of war is going to be literally a life and death decision for the Ukrainian leader, but waging it for another year or two is hardly a brighter prospect.

Trump secretly swapped planes in Turkey over Iran threat, report says
US President Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, an extraordinary move prompted by an Iranian assassination threat, the Washington Post reported Monday.

US President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month's NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday.
The Post said the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
Read moreTrump tempers fury at NATO summit after lashing out at key allies in Ankara
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a US official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel.
The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some US troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane – an Air Force C-32A – via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The US Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
While Trump was in Turkey, the US military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff".
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned US security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane – suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.
Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional investigation.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary".
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”
(FRANCE 24 with AP)

인텔이 유상증자 규모를 애초 150억달러에서 200억달러로 올렸다.
인텔은 "공모 자금은 일반적인 기업 자금으로 사용할 예정이며 여기에는 자본지출과 운전자본이 포함될 수 있지만 이에 국한되진 않는다"고 설명했다.
인텔은 지난 13일 아일랜드 렉슬립에 있는 '팹 34'에 50억유로를 투자한다고 밝힌 바 있다.
전체 내용을 이해하기 위해서는 기사 본문과 함께 읽어야 합니다.
송고 2026년08월11일 17시11분
구글 검색에서 연합뉴스 기사를 우선적으로 보여줍니다.
(서울=연합뉴스) 황정우 기자 = 인텔이 유상증자 규모를 애초 150억달러(약 21조3천억원)에서 200억달러(약 28조3천억원)로 올렸다.
인텔은 10일(현지시간) 성명을 통해 보통주 2억1천52만주에 대한 공모가격을 주당 95달러로 정했다며 이같이 밝혔다. 공모가는 10일 종가(97.52달러) 대비 2.6% 할인된 수준이다.
아울러 인텔은 주간사단에 3천1507만주를 초과배정옵션으로 배정했으며 공모가 12일 마무리된다고 덧붙였다.
앞서 블룸버그는 이번 증자에 1천억달러(약 141조원) 넘는 수요가 몰렸다고 전했다.
이번 인텔의 유상증자는 1971년 상장 이후 첫 대규모 주식 공모다. 주가 급등을 활용해 투자 등에 필요한 자금 확보에 나선 것으로 풀이된다. 올해 들어 인텔 주가는 164% 급등했다.
인텔은 "공모 자금은 일반적인 기업 자금으로 사용할 예정이며 여기에는 자본지출(CapEx)과 운전자본이 포함될 수 있지만 이에 국한되진 않는다"고 설명했다.
인텔은 지난 13일 아일랜드 렉슬립에 있는 '팹 34'에 50억유로(약 8조4천800억원)를 투자한다고 밝힌 바 있다. 팹 34를 현대화하고 생산량을 늘리는 한편 연구개발도 강화할 것이라고 설명했다.
 앞서 인텔은 2분기 실적 발표에서 올해 자본지출 예측치를 200억달러(약 28조3천억원)로 상향하면서 "내년까지 제품·파운드리 성장 지원을 위해 장비·청정실(클린룸)·기판 등에 대한 투자를 늘릴 계획"이라고 밝힌 바 있다.

Australia and Vietnam deepen strategic partnership on security, trade and energy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:11:17 UTC
17:11:17 KST

Australia and Vietnam on Tuesday agreed to deepen their comprehensive strategic partnership across defence, security, trade and clean energy during talks between Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Vietnamese President To Lam in Canberra.
The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a “peaceful, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific” that is free from coercion and where sovereignty is respected, according to a statement from the Australian Prime Minister’s Office.
They expressed concern over developments in the South China Sea and stressed the importance of freedom of navigation and overflight, peaceful resolution of disputes, and adherence to international law, particularly the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Albanese and Lam welcomed an updated joint vision for defence cooperation and agreed to expand collaboration in military training, maritime security, peacekeeping, search and rescue, information sharing and counterterrorism.
Cooperation in economy, tech
The two countries will also strengthen cooperation against cybercrime, online scams, drug trafficking, human trafficking and terrorism financing.
On economic ties, the leaders pledged to expand bilateral trade and investment, strengthen supply chains, and deepen cooperation in critical minerals.
They also welcomed agreements covering agriculture, vocational education, aviation, health, science and technology.
Both sides committed to accelerating renewable energy deployment and strengthening cooperation on climate change, maintaining their goal of reaching net-zero emissions by 2050.
The leaders also called for an immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar, unhindered humanitarian access, and inclusive dialogue, while reaffirming support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture.

엔화 환율 다시 160엔 육박…미일 동시개입 효과 끝났나
South Korea
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
17:11:17 KST
17:11:17 KST

日정부, 소비세 감면 따른 지방세수 감소 국고로 충당 검토
 (도쿄=연합뉴스) 조성미 특파원 = 일본 엔화 환율이 미·일의 이례적 동시 환율 개입 이후에도 다시 약세가 이어지며 개입 이전 수준으로 복귀했다.
 11일 현지 언론에 따르면 현지시간 10일 뉴욕 외환시장에서 엔/달러 환율은 159.25엔 수준에서 거래를 마쳤다. 
 엔/달러 환율은 장 중 한때 159.36엔까지 오르며 엔화 가치는 일본 정부가 미국과 공조해 엔화 매수 개입에 나선 지난달 31일 이후 최저치를 기록했다.
 일본에서는 이날 '산의 날' 공휴일을 맞아 금융시잗이 휴장한 가운데 거래자들이 추이를 관망하고 있다.
 호르무즈 해협을 둘러싼 불확실성이 지속되는 가운데 원유 선물 가격이 상승한 것이 원유 수입량 대부분을 중동에 의존하는 일본 통화 환율에 부담으로 작용한 것으로 분석됐다.
 여기에 미국의 물가 상승 압력이 커질 것이라는 전망에 따라 미국 장기 금리가 상승하면서 미일 금리 차가 더 커질 것이라는 전망이 엔화 매도와 달러화 매수를 부추겼다.
 미일 금리 차이나 일본 다카이치 사나에 내각의 확장 재정 기조 등 펀더멘털(경제 기초여건)이 변하지 않는 한 미일 당국의 환율 개입 효과가 오래 지속되기 어렵다는 시장 전문가들의 분석이 나오고 있다.
 
 이런 가운데 내년 4월부터 식료품 소비세율을 현행 8%에서 1%로 2년간 인하하는 방안을 추진 중인 다카이치 내각이 세율 인하에 따른 지방의 세수 감소분을 국고로 보전하는 방안을 검토 중이라고 교도통신이 전했다.
 지방의 일시적인 세수 감소를 보전하기 위해 정부가 지방자치단체에 교부하는 지방특례교부금을 활용하는 방안이 유력하게 거론되고 있다.
 일본 정부는 식료품 소비세율 한시적 인하로 발생하는 연간 지방세수 감소액을 지방소비세 1조엔(약 8조9천억원), 지방교부세 7천억엔(약 6조2천억원)으로 추산하는 것으로 전해졌다.
 식료품 소비세율 감면에 따른 세수 부족분을 메우기 위해 일본 정부가 적자 국채를 늘릴 가능성이 거론되고 있다.
 다만, 다카이치 총리는 재정 보조금 재검토와 세외수입 확보 등으로 감세에 대응하고 적자 국채 발행에 의존하지 않겠다는 입장을 표명 중이다.

중국서 2천300년 된 술 발견…청동 항아리 속 3.7리터 보존
South Korea
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
17:10:58 KST
17:10:58 KST

중국의 전국시대 무덤 유적지에서 2천300년 된 술이 발견됐다.
11일 홍콩 사우스차이나모닝포스트에 따르면 중국 북서부 닝샤 후이족 자치구 구위안시의 전국시대 무덤에서 청동으로 된 항아리가 발굴됐다.
항아리는 중국 전국시대 진나라 장성 유적에서 약 2㎞ 떨어진 산자바오 무덤에서 나왔다.
전체 내용을 이해하기 위해서는 기사 본문과 함께 읽어야 합니다.
송고 2026년08월11일 17시10분
구글 검색에서 연합뉴스 기사를 우선적으로 보여줍니다.
(서울=연합뉴스) 권숙희 기자 = 중국의 전국시대 무덤 유적지에서 2천300년 된 술이 발견됐다.
11일 홍콩 사우스차이나모닝포스트(SCMP)에 따르면 중국 북서부 닝샤 후이족 자치구 구위안시의 전국시대(기원전 403년∼기원전 221년) 무덤에서 청동으로 된 항아리가 발굴됐다.
항아리는 중국 전국시대 진나라 장성(長城) 유적에서 약 2㎞ 떨어진 산자바오 무덤에서 나왔다.
밀봉이 거의 완벽한 상태였던 항아리에는 곡주로 추정되는 액체 약 3.7리터(ℓ)가 담겨 있었다.
이 항아리는 닝샤 고고학연구소가 2024년 3월 시작한 산자바오 무덤 발굴 과정에서 발견됐다.
연구진은 전국시대 무덤 183기를 발굴했으며 이 가운데 179기는 진나라 문화에 속하는 것이었다.
이 무덤이 장성 일대 방어 시설에 주둔하던 병사들과 주민들이 이용한 공동묘지였을 가능성이 있는 것으로 연구진은 추정했다.
이중 39호 무덤에서 출토된 마늘 머리 모양의 주둥이가 달린 청동 항아리에서 액체 3.74ℓ가 검출됐다.
액체에서는 유기산 및 그 유도체, 아미노산 및 그 유도체, 탄수화물 등 모두 24종의 화합물이 검출됐다.
유기산의 분포 양상이 인공적으로 숙성시킨 중국의 황주와 일치했다. 이를 통해 이 액체가 포도주 같은 과실주가 아니라 곡물을 원료로 한 곡주라는 사실이 드러났다.
연구진이 잔류물을 분석한 결과 전분의 92% 이상이 기장에서 유래한 것으로 밝혀졌다. 나머지 전분은 밀과 보리에서 나온 것이었다.
기장은 물을 적게 필요로 하는 곡물로, 중국 북부에서 약 1만년 전부터 식용됐다.
닝샤 문물고고연구소의 산자바오 무덤 발굴 프로젝트 책임자 왕샤오양은 중국 현지 매체와의 인터뷰에서 "이 청동 항아리는 안쪽에는 직물을 대고 바깥쪽에는 유기질 점토를 바르는 이중 밀봉 기법을 사용했다"며 "덕분에 2천여년 넘은 술이 거의 온전하게 보존됐고 증발된 양도 적었다"고 말했다.
이러한 발견에 대한 연구 성과는 국제학술지 고고과학저널(Journal of Archaeological Science) 6월호에 게재돼 최근 알려졌다.
연구 제1저자인 시베이대 박사과정 천루루는 "이번 연구는 진나라 시대 사람들이 곡물을 어떻게 이용하고 어떤 양조기술을 사용했는지를 명확하게 보여준다"라면서 "고대 중국의 양조 기술을 복원하고 발전 과정을 보다 세밀하게 밝히는 데도 도움이 될 것"이라고 밝혔다.

Clarkson’s Farm producer shares hit show’s A-list celebrity fans
Jeremy Clarkson’s beloved series has three very famous viewers
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Clarkson’s Farm is one of the most successful shows on Prime Video – and it has at least three A-list fans, according to its producer.
Andy Wilman has said that the series’ “most interesting fan” is Bernie Ecclestone, the former head of Formula 1, who he claims talks about farming with Jeremy Clarkson whenever he sees him at the Grand Prix. Eccleston runs his own cattle farm in Brazil.
“They’re on a grid with a Ferrari next to them and they’re like: ‘The thing about your Friesian cows is . . . ’ and all this sort of stuff,” Wilman told The Sun.
Elsewhere, Lost in Translation director Sofia Coppola – daughter of Godfather filmmaker Francis Ford Coppola – also tunes in to new episodes, as does David Beckham, who is a superfan.
Wilman, who also produces The Grand Tour, claimed that Beckham visited Diddly Squat and “was so starstruck” when he met farmhand Gerald Cooper, and ran to get a selfie with him.
Clarkson’s Farm details the TV personality’s efforts to run the 1,000-acre Oxfordshire holding, which he has been running since 2019. The latest season featured a knees-up in his accompanying boozer – but the celebrities in attendance were cut from the episode.
Clarkson opened his watering hole, The Farmer’s Dog, in August 2024 and, a few months later, held his first gig, booking Irish band The Corrs.
While the trio, made up of siblings Andrea, Sharon and Jim, were shown performing in the second episode of Clarkson’s Farm season five, there were a few faces missing from scenes – namely celebrity couple Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi.
Former chat show host DeGeneres and Arrested Development star de Rossi were invited by Clarkson and his girlfriend, Lisa Hogan, after they moved to the Cotswolds from America.
At the time, the pair shared footage from the event, where The Corrs played hits including “Breathless” and “Runaway”. However, shortly afterwards, the videos disappeared from their social media pages.
Other celebrities in attendance at The Farmer’s Dog gig who didn’t make the cut included “Torn” singer Natalie Imbruglia and James Blunt, known for his songs “You’re Beautiful” and “Goodbye My Lover”. They watched the gig from a balcony overlooking the stage.

While it’s a sure bet they’ll rival the original hosts’ car knowledge, they’ll be hoping to emulate their chemistry for a new era – and the trailer has provided the first evidence of whether they have succeeded.
In the new series, the presenters will tackle motoring’s most absurd questions across some of the world’s most challenging terrains. As part of the new episodes, they will cross the Angolan desert in track cars and explore Malaysia’s vibrant car culture.

Indonesian officials race to contain wildfires as dozens of schools shut
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:08:13 UTC
17:08:13 KST

Indonesian officials race to contain wildfires as dozens of schools shut
Cloud-seeding aircraft have been deployed as dozens of schools remain closed due to poor air quality.
Authorities in Indonesia are scrambling to contain wildfires that have burned through more than 100,000 hectares (247,000 acres) of land and led to the deployment of nearly 50,000 firefighters.
Dozens of schools remain closed for a second day on Tuesday due to poor air quality caused by the blazes.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3June and July hottest on record in Western Europe, monitor says
- list 2 of 3Indonesia closes national park in East Java as wildfire expands
- list 3 of 3Wildfires burn across Indonesia as officials cite El Nino as a cause
In West Kalimantan on the island of Borneo, which Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, the mayor of Pontianak ordered schools closed due to the smoke wafting over the city from fires elsewhere.
Children will learn from home for as long as air quality remains poor, Mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono said in a statement on Monday.
El Nino has contributed to dry conditions across the archipelago, increasing the risk of wildfires, as officials prioritise tackling the blazes in six provinces: Riau, Jambi and South Sumatra on Sumatra island, as well as West Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan on Borneo island.
Addressing reporters on Monday, Chief Security Minister Djamari Chaniago warned that the arid conditions increased the likelihood of the fires spreading.
“We are on alert because the weather conditions really make it possible for these fires to become larger,” Chaniago said.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns.
In India and Southeast Asia, it typically causes drier conditions.
Authorities are trying to induce rain through cloud seeding. Chemicals such as silver iodide and salt are sprayed into clouds as part of the technique, which can increase rainfall by up to 15 percent.
However, Chaniago cautioned that authorities are struggling to find enough rain clouds to target.
“That is why we closely monitor even small changes in the weather. Whenever something is likely to produce rain clouds, we immediately carry [cloud seeding operations] out,” he said.
On Tuesday, firefighters were among more than 150 personnel working to extinguish what remained of a blaze at Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java province. The fire, which has destroyed about 900 hectares (2,200 acres) of land since starting nine days ago, has been mostly brought under control. It now covers about 2 hectares (5 acres).
More than a dozen aircraft have been deployed across Indonesia as part of cloud-seeding efforts, along with 43 helicopters assisting firefighters on the ground.
More than 107,000 hectares (264,000 acres) of land across the country were affected by blazes from January to June, according to Ministry of Forestry data. That marks an increase of 110 percent compared with the same period in 2023, when El Nino last affected Indonesia.

When I started in EastEnders, there were people who were like, ‘You know, there are people out there who really can’t tell the difference between what they see on telly and real life, and because of the character you’re playing, you’re going to get a lot of shit, and you might need police protection’.

“If I could sing, I wouldn’t be an actor. If I could sing, I would have been in a band in the 1990s.”

Why is the internet accusing Anne Hathaway of wearing a fake pregnancy belly?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:06:42 UTC
17:06:42 KST

Social media users have claimed that Anne Hathaway was wearing a fake pregnancy belly on the red carpet for the premiere of 'The End Of Oak Street'. This has led the actress to respond and further proves that the chronically online really need a hobby.
Everyone's talking about how Tom Holland and Zendaya are having a great year, but let's not forget that Anne Hathaway is making her mark on 2026.
The 43-year-old Oscar-winning actress has been one of the most bankable stars of the year, with roles in The Devil Wears Prada 2 and The Odyssey, and has also starred in one of our favourite films of the year so far – the underseen Mother Mary.
She's now on press tour duties for her latest role in David Robert Mitchell's The End Of Oak Street, a sci-fi survival film produced by J.J. Abrams - and therefore rumoured to be a part of his Cloverfield anthology universe.
As if that wasn't enough to celebrate, Hathaway is currently pregnant with her third child.
But because we can't have nice things, the internet went and made it weird.
We say weird, we mean idiotic - proving once again that deeply missed author Umberto Eco was right when he said that the tragedy of the internet "is that it has promoted the village idiot to the level of bearer of truth".
And a loud one at that.
Hathaway attended the world premiere of The End Of Oak Street at the Steven J. Ross Theater in Burbank in California, wearing a custom look by Atelier Prabal Gurung, consisting of low-rise jeans and a stylish crop top which showed off her baby bump.
As per usual, Hathaway looked radiant, but certain social media users decided it was time to disprove Darwinism by accusing the actress of not only looking "bizarre" and "tacky" but wearing a fake pregnancy belly.
Following a viral post on X (where else?) from an account titled “21”, commenters pointed out that there was something "off" with Hathaway's stomach.
“Looks like a fake stomach. The belly button looks unreal,” one person commented. Another posted that it looked like "a prosthetic bump", while one user chimed in by writing: "As someone who has kids, her belly looks like those fake ones they use in movies."
Charming and not at all unwarranted.
The conspiracy theory went so viral that Hathaway was forced to respond, bringing classiness and humour to a pigsty.
She posted a video from the evening on Instagram and titled it: “Fake hair, real bump.”
Sadly - but somewhat predictably - that wasn't the end of it.
As if it wasn't distasteful enough to body shame and pass judgement on a pregnant woman's body, some commentators started blaming Hathaway's stylist for the apparently "unflattering wardrobe malfunction".
“Unflattering styling for a beautiful pregnant woman,” one wannabe fashionista wrote, while another commented: “Pregnancy is beautiful, but this is a stylist fail."
Now, to each their own when it comes to style and thoughts on low-rise jeans - but there are some crucial elements to take into consideration.
Firstly, why is this such a big deal?
Secondly, no two pregnancy bumps are identical. Grow up.
Thirdly, when you're carrying the weight of a person inside you, you should be able to wear whatever makes you happy and comfortable without fear of either judgement or baseless theories accusing you of faking your pregnancy. Like Demi Moore posing for Annie Leibovitz on Vanity Fair in 1991 and Rihanna proudly revealing her pregnancy during the Super Bowl Halftime Show in 2023, Hathaway isn't hiding her physical transformation and is choosing to celebrate it by not treating it as "unglamorous" or "weird", as certain folk on social media choose to label it. Their reaction smacks of still engrained stigma when it comes to maternity and women's changing bodies.
Then there's the wider context to think about.
Anne Hathaway is married to actor Adam Shulman and before having her first two children in 2016 and 2019, she experienced a miscarriage in 2015. Worse, she suffered her miscarriage while starring in the one-woman play, Grounded, in which she had to act out childbirth every night.
Hathaway has been open about this and recently spoke to late night host Seth Meyers about how shocked she was to have got pregnant so easily given her age and after fertility challenges.
Announcing her second pregnancy in 2019, she also shared the challenges of conception: “For everyone going through infertility and conception hell, please know it was not a straight line to either of my pregnancies. Sending you extra love.”
While it might still be too much to ask for the chronically online to embrace body positivity for all, maybe they could redirect all that energy towards more meaningful matters. Or stop depriving that village of their idiot.
Anne Hathaway stars in The End of Oak Street, which is out this week. Stay tuned to Euronews Culture for our full review.

Trump demands Iran pay compensation as hopes fade for Hormuz deal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:05:00 UTC
17:05:00 KST

U.S. President Donald Trump escalated a standoff with Iran on Monday by demanding compensation from Tehran for deaths and destruction linked to decades of conflict, after Iranian officials said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Washington meets a series of conditions.
The competing demands could further complicate efforts to reach an agreement to reopen the strategic waterway, which has been effectively blocked since the war began and has contributed to higher energy prices.
Trump said Iran's demand for compensation for damage caused by U.S. and Israeli attacks had only recently emerged. He responded by saying Tehran should also pay for Americans and others killed or wounded in conflicts and attacks that Washington has linked to Iran or Iranian-backed groups.
"We're going to ask for money for the damage they've done over a 50-year period," Trump told reporters at the White House.
In a Truth Social post, Trump said he had instructed his representatives to include compensation in any future negotiations with Tehran.
"Iran should be responsible for the damages and death caused to the people of Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and Gaza!" Trump wrote.
Trump also called for compensation for families of Iranian protesters killed during the government's crackdown. He cited a figure of about 52,000 deaths, although rights groups have reported substantially lower figures.
He also said Iran should compensate families of 17 U.S. sailors killed in the 2000 bombing of the USS Cole in Yemen. The attack was carried out by al-Qaida and has not been attributed to Iran.
Washington has separately blamed Iran-backed groups for the deaths of hundreds of Americans, including 241 U.S. military personnel killed in the 1983 bombing of a Marine barracks in Beirut and at least 603 U.S. troops killed in Iraq between 2003 and 2011.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until Washington ends its blockade of Iranian ports, lifts economic sanctions and releases frozen Iranian assets.
Tehran is also demanding compensation for damage caused by the U.S.-Israeli bombardment.
"It is up to the U.S. side to stop and make amends for its illegal and destructive actions," Baghaei said.
The Strait of Hormuz has become the central issue in the standoff. Before the war, roughly one-fifth of the world's traded oil and a significant share of global liquefied natural gas passed through the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.
The disruption has pushed energy prices higher and raised inflation concerns, increasing pressure on Trump ahead of November's midterm elections. Oil prices settled about 5% higher Monday as Trump's demands reduced hopes for a deal to restore shipping.
Iran said talks with Oman over new shipping arrangements were progressing. Baghaei said the two sides had agreed on a map for a proposed shipping route, although technical issues remained.
The discussions also covered safe navigation, environmental protection, maritime services and efforts to combat crime. U.S. officials have rejected any arrangement that would allow Iran to charge fees for access to the strait.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said the country's new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, had called for unity as the Islamic Republic faces sanctions, economic pressure and the consequences of the war.
Pezeshkian told state television that he spent nearly seven hours with Khamenei discussing living costs, employment, housing and problems caused by U.S. sanctions.
But he said Khamenei's main message was preventing internal divisions.
"All of the enemy's plans are aimed at creating division," Pezeshkian said. "What we have to do is prevent divisions from emerging."
It was only the second time Pezeshkian has publicly said he met with Khamenei since the younger Khamenei was appointed supreme leader in March after a U.S.-Israeli strike killed his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The new leader is believed to have been wounded and has not appeared publicly since.
Iran also appointed Mohsen Rezaei, a longtime Revolutionary Guard commander and adviser to Khamenei, as head of the Supreme National Security Council.
Rezaei, 71, led the Revolutionary Guard from 1981 to 1997. He has threatened serious consequences for U.S. forces if Washington does not lift its blockade of Iranian ports.
The Institute for the Study of War said Rezaei appeared willing to negotiate with Washington to advance Iran's objectives, including control over the Strait of Hormuz, while showing little willingness to offer concessions.
The conflict continued to reverberate across the Middle East.
In the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the Israeli military declared the Christian-majority town of Taybeh a closed military zone, saying the move was intended to keep Israeli settlers and other nonresidents away.
The decision followed months of reported arson, vandalism and settler incursions onto private and village property.
The military said Palestinian residents and journalists would be allowed to enter unless they pose a security threat. According to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Health Ministry, at least 87 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli settlers or soldiers in 2026.
In Yemen, Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacked the Red Sea port town of Mokha on Sunday, killing seven people and wounding 30, according to Yemen's Defense Ministry. Four of those killed were military personnel and three were civilians.
Fighting continued Monday near Taiz. The Houthis said artillery shelling killed a 13-year-old child and wounded another.
The attack was among the largest waves of Houthi strikes against positions held by Yemen's internationally recognized government since a 2022 truce.
The violence has added uncertainty to regional shipping as the crisis around Hormuz increases attention on the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
