'Extreme heat' warning issued for parts of England on Thursday
The Met Office has issued an amber heat warning for large parts of England on Thursday, covering areas including London, St Albans, Cambridge, Oxford, Milton Keynes, Peterborough, Leicester, Birmingham, Nottingham, Lincoln and Sheffield. It will be in place from 9am to midnight on Thursday.
The Met Office warned that the “extreme heat” warning will likely cause “adverse” health effects to people vulnerable to extreme heat, adding that there could be delays to travel and that some “heat sensitive systems and equipment may fail”, leading to potential power cuts at some homes and businesses.
“Following a warm night, a spell of very hot weather will affect England on Thursday,” the Met Office said.
“The highest temperatures will be in parts of the east, southeast and the Midlands, where 37 or even 38 celsius could be reached. This may lead to impacts on transport, infrastructure and health.”
The advice is to stay hydrated, keep out of the sun if possible, wear sunscreen if you are outside, avoid any exercise between 11am-3pm when the sun is strongest and close curtains in rooms that face the sun.
Forestry England has issued an update on the situation in the New Forest where firefighters are in the third day of tackling a fire.
PA Media reports the agency said it will work with local groups to support animals impacted by the fire once the incident is over and urged people to continue to avoid affected areas. A spokesperson said:
With diversions and road closures in place, we would like to remind everyone driving through the forest that animals can be close to or on the roads at any time of the day or night. Please drive with care and within the speed limit.
Our team remain on site to assist the emergency services and are continuing to cut additional fire breaks.
We understand how upsetting this incident is and the concern for wildlife. We would like to thank everyone who has kindly offered assistance and support.
When it is safe to do so our team will assess the impact of the fire and work closely with local groups and the community to support wildlife and the wider recovery of the affected area.
National Highways has said that junctions 21A to 22 of the M25 have been reopened after the carriageways were closed following a fire.
“The M25 has reopened in both directions with 40 mph speed restrictions, following instructions from fire crews. Due to the volume of traffic, it may take time for congestion to clear,” National Highways wrote in a brief statement posted on social media.
Hertfordshire Fire and Rescue was called to a fire in Ventura Park, Old Parkbury Lane, Colney Street, in St Albans this morning in response to reports of a fire at a large industrial unit.
Both carriageways of the M25 between junctions 22 and 21A were subsequently closed due to what National Highways described as a risk of a “secondary explosion, along with smoke and debris affecting the carriageway”.
There were no immediate reports of any casualties or injuries, and the extent of the damage remains unclear. It is also unclear how exactly the blaze started.
We are seeing reports that thousands of homes have been affected by a disruption to water supplies in areas of London and Essex.
Sky News reports that about 10,000 homes are without water or experiencing low pressure in the Chigwell area, with issues first occurring on Saturday evening. A second water main reportedly burst on Chigwell Road in South Woodford on Sunday morning.
In an update this morning, Thames Water apologised to customers whose water supply had been affected, adding that its teams are “working tirelessly” to fix the broken pipes, citing progress with repairs on Chigwell Road and Daisy Road.
It said:
We’re sorry to customers who’s water supply is still affected this morning. Our teams are working tirelessly in extremely difficult circumstances to fix the broken pipes in the area. Unfortunately they are proving to be more difficult to repair than at first thought.
Pipe damage affected properties across E4, E10, E11, E17, E18, IG2, IG4, IG5, IG6, IG7, IG8, IG9, IG10 and RM4, with many experiencing low water pressure or no running water. Thames Water said it will be providing another update by 1pm this afternoon.
The Guardian’s environment editor, Fiona Harvey, has written a useful explainer about the UK public services that are struggling in the extreme weather. You can read it in full here:
There’s only one solution in the end to the drought now declared across most of England and that’s rain, says Hannah Cloke, professor of hydrology at the University of Reading.
“While water companies and regulators have a range of measures available to manage demand, like restrictions and hosepipe bans, these are aimed at slowing the rate at which water resources are depleted,” she said.
“It will not end the drought itself. Meaningful recovery in the months and even years ahead will require sustained rainfall over many weeks or months.” But she warned of potential flash flooding when rain falls on baked ground. She said:
An important consequence of drought is that very dry soils can become less able to absorb rainfall when it does arrive. This can increase surface runoff and can even contribute to localised flash flooding, particularly if rain falls intensely over a short period.
The current situation highlights the need to improve long-term resilience to both drought and flood risk as climate variability increases, and shows one more damaging impact of the burning of fossil fuels.
The climate crisis is increasing both summer heatwaves and winter rainfall in the UK, meaning new reservoirs to store water between seasons should be a priority.
Last year, the government ordered the building of two major reservoirs, the first to be built in England for more than 30 years. However, the reservoirs in East Anglia and Lincolnshire will not be ready until 2036 and 2040 respectively.
Another seven new large reservoirs are planned to be built by 2050, in Oxfordshire, Suffolk, Kent, East Sussex, the West Midlands and two in Somerset. Work is already under way at a further site in Hampshire.
'Extreme heat' warning issued for parts of England on Thursday
The Met Office has issued an amber heat warning for large parts of England on Thursday, covering areas including London, St Albans, Cambridge, Oxford, Milton Keynes, Peterborough, Leicester, Birmingham, Nottingham, Lincoln and Sheffield. It will be in place from 9am to midnight on Thursday.
The Met Office warned that the “extreme heat” warning will likely cause “adverse” health effects to people vulnerable to extreme heat, adding that there could be delays to travel and that some “heat sensitive systems and equipment may fail”, leading to potential power cuts at some homes and businesses.
“Following a warm night, a spell of very hot weather will affect England on Thursday,” the Met Office said.
“The highest temperatures will be in parts of the east, southeast and the Midlands, where 37 or even 38 celsius could be reached. This may lead to impacts on transport, infrastructure and health.”
The advice is to stay hydrated, keep out of the sun if possible, wear sunscreen if you are outside, avoid any exercise between 11am-3pm when the sun is strongest and close curtains in rooms that face the sun.
The so-called “fire wave” under way in the UK is the most widespread the country has ever seen, with the combination of wet winters and prolonged heatwaves exacerbating the risk.
Several wildfires have broken out in the UK over recent weeks amid the hot and dry weather.
These include large blazes at Holme Fen, a peatland nature reservenear Peterborough, Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, Headon Warren on the Isle of Wight, Llanwonno in the Rhondda Valleys, south Wales and the Cairngorms national park in Scotland.
Firefighters work to contain New Forest fire for third day
Firefighters are beginning a third day of tackling a fire in the New Forest in Hampshire. Forestry England says the fire is under control but efforts to contain it could last for several days.
Hampshire Fire and Rescue Service, assisted by neighbouring services, initially scrambled 26 fire engines alongside water carriers to the eastbound A31 after receiving reports that a van had caught fire on Sunday evening.
The fire service said the fire spread from the vehicle to the central reservation before progressing into nearby heathland. In a statement, it said:
Crews have worked tirelessly throughout the night, a change in wind direction provided a challenge to the firefighting operations but thanks to the efforts of firefighters we are managing to contain the fire.
We have been using a mix of fire engines and off-road vehicles to damp down and cool the edges of the area involved in the fire to prevent spread and escalation …
Overnight we had a slightly reduced presence with seven fire engines on site plus water carriers, off road vehicles and support vehicles but are planning to increase this for a larger scale attack today.
The A31 remains closed – and National Highways described “significant” damage to the road surface, road safety barrier and boundary fencing that will require repairs once it is safe to do so.
Farmers have reported their earliest harvests in 20 years, with reduced yields, while reservoir levels have fallen to 69% – 11.6% lower than expected for this time of year.
Paul Tompkins, the deputy president of the National Farmers’ Union, said that with no meaningful rain forecast in the coming weeks, the situation for farmers was increasingly concerning. He said:
Many farmers have completed the earliest harvest on record, with poor yields in key crops reported in some areas of the country.
Livestock and dairy farmers are already using winter feed because grass has stopped growing, while growers are working hard to keep fruit and vegetables watered, but many are struggling to access the water they need.
The government said it was considering ways to give more support to the farming sector. The water minister, Emma Hardy, said this would include making it easier to build on-farm reservoirs.
The Met Office has shared two images taken from space that reveal the stark contrast in much of the UK’s landscape between 23 May and yesterday. They capture how an exceptionally dry and hot period turned lots of once green land brown.
Heat health alerts now in place across whole of England
Amber heat health alerts are now in effect across all regions of England, aside from the north east, which has been given a yellow alert, up until Friday evening. You can keep up to date with the latest weather health alerts here.
As we mentioned in the opening post, amber heat health alerts come into force across most of England from 9am today and will last until 9pm on Friday.
As well as a rise in deaths and likely “significant” impacts across health and social care services, here are some of the other risks associated with the amber category, as outlined by the UK Health Security Agency:
internal temperatures in hospitals and care homes may exceed the recommended threshold for clinical risk assessment
the heat affecting the ability of the workforce to deliver services
indoor environments overheating increasing the risk to some vulnerable people
issues managing medicines
increased demand for power exceeding capacity
possible travel delays
water‑related incidents may increase, including risks from cold‑water shock and drowning
Amber heat health alerts have been issued for all regions in England, except the north-east, which mean significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures, according to the UK’s Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The alerts stretch from 9am on Tuesday until 9pm on Friday.
The north-east will be under a yellow health alert, which is less intense than the amber category but is still linked to a rise in deaths, particularly among those aged 65 and over or with health conditions, and a likely increase in demand for health services.
The alerts come a day after four more regions of England were officially declared to be in drought: the East Midlands, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire, Kent and East Sussex, and Solent and the South Downs.
They joined seven English regions, alongside the whole of Wales, already under drought status since last month: East Anglia, Hertfordshire and London, Thames Valley, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, Devon and Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire and south Gloucestershire).
The Environment Agency said 71.3% of England is experiencing “flash drought”, as a dry start to August followed the country’s driest July on record.
On Tuesday, highs of 29C in Cardiff, 28C in Manchester and 25C in London are forecast before temperatures soar to the mid-30s in some areas on Thursday, according to the Met Office, with temperatures possibly exceeding 36C in some places.

14 illegal miners dead, scores injured at disused South Africa mine, police say
JOHANNESBURG, Aug 11 - South African police said on Tuesday that 14 illegal miners had died and scores of others had been injured at a disused mine near Rustenburg in the North West province.
Police did not give more details. A senior provincial police official is on the way to the scene.
Illegal mining has plagued South Africa for decades through small-time pilfering and organised criminal networks.
Typically, undocumented miners move into mines abandoned by commercial miners and seek to extract whatever is left. Some are under the control of violent criminal gangs.
Illegal mining costs the government and mining industry hundreds of millions of dollars annually in lost sales, taxes and royalties. REUTERS

Owned by businessman Mikhail Gutseriyev’s Safmar Group, Orsknefteorgsintez is one of Russia’s leading refineries with an annual processing capacity of 6.6 million metric tons. The facility produces about 30 types of petroleum products, including gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, bitumen and fuel oil.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 396 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Monday night and Tuesday morning.

Jon Cypher death: Cinderella and Hill Street Blues star dies at 94
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:37:36 BST
16:37:36 KST

Jon Cypher death: Cinderella and Hill Street Blues star dies at 94
Actor was best known for playing police chief Fletcher Daniels in acclaimed American drama Hill Street Blues
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Jon Cypher, best known for playing the calculating police chief Fletcher Daniels in the acclaimed American drama Hill Street Blues, has died aged 94.
Cypher died at his home in Twin Creeks, Central Point, Oregon, with his wife of 40 years, author Carol Rosin, by his side, according to his obituary in Ashland News.
No cause of death was provided.
He will be laid to rest in Ashland on Tuesday in a burial that “reflects his wish to return to nature”.
He starred as Prince Christopher opposite Julie Andrews in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella, a 1957 CBS live production that became a landmark in US television history.
The broadcast, which aired in colour on 31 March that year, attracted almost 107 million viewers, accounting for over 60 per cent of American households at the time, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
Cypher’s best-known role came over two decades later, when he joined Hill Street Blues as Chief Fletcher Daniels.
He appeared in 71 episodes of the NBC series between 1981 and 1987, frequently finding himself at odds with Daniel J Travanti’s Captain Frank Furillo.
The series, which followed officers at a fictional police station, became one of the defining American television dramas of the 1980s.
It won 26 Emmy awards, including four consecutive wins for outstanding drama series from 1981 to 1984, according to the Los Angeles Times.
He made his Broadway debut in The Disenchanted in 1958 and went on to appear in productions including The Night of the Iguana, Man of La Mancha, The Great White Hope, and 1776. His final Broadway appearance was in the 1996 production of Big.
Cypher became a familiar face on soap operas and primetime television, with credits in As the World Turns, General Hospital, Santa Barbara, Knots Landing, and Dynasty, as well as guest appearances in The Rockford Files, Murder, She Wrote, JAG, Walker, Texas Ranger, and Law & Order.
He had another major television role towards the end of his career in the CBS sitcom Major Dad, where he played Brigadier General Marcus Craig for the final three seasons, appearing in 69 episodes between 1990 and 1993.
In the 1987 fantasy film Masters of the Universe starring Dolph Lundgren in the titular role, Cypher played He-Man’s heroic ally Man-at-Arms.
He later said he had been reluctant to take the role because Man-at-Arms had only a small part in the original script. However, director Gary Goddard said he planned to expand the character, and Cypher subsequently rewrote one of the scenes himself.
“Gary was true to his word and, in fact, I actually rewrote one of the scenes and Gary liked it and added it on the very day I brought it in,” Cypher said in a 2013 interview with Motu Movie.
He also appeared in Valdez Is Coming alongside Burt Lancaster in 1971 as well as in Spontaneous Combustion and Strictly Business.
His family said that Cypher sang opera in four languages and “was known to burst out in song, bringing joy to every event”.
In 2019, he published If You’re Not Depressed You Oughta Be in Therapy, a collection of 99 limericks and commentary.
In a 2014 interview with the Ashland Theatre, he described acting as a career where performers were “always being judged, by critics, by the audience”, and said anyone considering it should be prepared to “pick yourself up many, many, many times”.
“When you’re an actor, it’s what you do,” he said, “as long as you can do it.”

'Evil incarnate': Hunter Biden takes aim at Netanyahu in Tucker Carlson interview
Hunter Biden has described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as "evil incarnate" and said that Israeli-linked figures were involved in circulating his personal material ahead of the 2020 US presidential election, as he joined conservative commentator Tucker Carlson in a sweeping attack on Israel's influence over US politics.
Biden made the remarks during a wide-ranging interview on Monday on The Tucker Carlson Show, hosted by the former Fox News host and influential conservative commentator who has become an increasingly vocal critic of Israel and US military involvement in the region.
"If pointing out that Benjamin Netanyahu is evil incarnate is antisemitic, then I don't know what to tell people anymore," Biden said.
He also defended Carlson against accusations of antisemitism, telling him: "I know 100 percent that you’re not antisemitic", adding that such accusations were being used to shut down criticism of Netanyahu.
The two men also discussed the controversy surrounding Biden's laptop, which emerged shortly before the 2020 presidential election and became a major focus of Republican attacks against Biden and his father.
Biden suggested that several groups had been involved in obtaining or distributing his personal material, including Russian-Ukrainian actors, Americans and what he described as a "Netanyahu operation centre, the Israeli side".
Carlson also said that Israeli figures had been involved in spreading false claims about what was contained on Biden’s laptop.
The conservative commentator said a person "connected to Netanyahu" had approached a producer on his former Fox News programme and claimed the laptop contained abusive images of children.
"That came from the Israelis," Carlson said, before adding: "They were behind that."
No evidence has emerged that the laptop contained abusive images of children, despite conspiracy theories that circulated online following its emergence.
The laptop controversy erupted in October 2020, weeks before Joe Biden defeated Donald Trump in the presidential election, after the New York Post published emails and other material it said came from a computer Hunter Biden had left at a Delaware repair shop.
Some emails contained in copies of the laptop data were later independently authenticated, but the material also became the subject of numerous unsubstantiated claims about Biden and his family.
Carlson, who at the time hosted one of Fox News's most-watched programmes, was among the conservative media personalities who repeatedly covered the controversy and attacked Biden over his personal life and years-long struggle with drug and alcohol addiction.
During Monday's interview, Carlson expressed regret for some of those attacks.
When Biden jokingly reminded him of "the things that you said about me", Carlson replied: "Deep regret".
Despite occupying opposing sides of US politics for years, Biden and Carlson also found common ground over Washington’s foreign policy and the US relationship with Israel.
Biden praised Republican Congressman Thomas Massie and former congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene, both of whom have broken with sections of their party over foreign policy, saying he was pleased that some conservatives had "woken up".
He also agreed with Carlson's criticism of Fox News over its approach to the war with Iran.
Carlson, once a prominent supporter of Trump, has become an increasingly vocal critic of the president over foreign policy, particularly Washington’s relationship with Israel and the US war with Iran.
Biden also used the interview to attack Trump, describing him as one of the most consequential political figures in modern US history "all for ill" and accusing him of deepening the country’s political divisions.
"I believe Trump is central to why this disease has gone from a local epidemic to a pandemic in the United States of America," Biden said.

US prosecutors want Tate brothers to remain in custody over ‘flight risk’

Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:35:22 BST

US prosecutors want Tate brothers to remain in custody over ‘flight risk’
The UK has until mid-September to provide evidence to the State Department to support extradition
- Bookmark
Prosecutors have said they want Andrew and Tristan Tate to remain in federal custody, arguing on Monday that the brothers are a flight risk and a danger to the community, as they fight extradition to the United Kingdom, where the brothers are accused of rape and sex trafficking.
Three days after defense attorneys filed a motion for release, prosecutors filed their response in Miami federal court, where a hearing on Thursday will determine if the brothers should stay in jail or be released during what could be a monthslong extradition process.
The brothers have repeatedly denied wrongdoing.
The detention hearing is likely to be the first time the Tates leave the Federal Detention Center in Miami since making a brief court appearance two days after their July 18 arrest. The Tates have become among the world’s most polarizing internet personalities with their promotion of wealth, male dominance and misogyny through their social media empire. The new allegations are the latest in the Tates' long-running international legal saga spanning the U.S., Britain and Romania.
According to the U.S. Attorney's Office filing, the Tates should be detained pending their extradition hearing because they cannot overcome the strong presumption against bail in international extradition cases.
The serious pending UK charges involving human trafficking and violent rapes and assaults against multiple victims, along with allegations in Romania that the Tates attempted to intimidate witnesses, present a clear public safety concern, prosecutors say.
“That the Tates also claim to maintain multiple passports and identities, have access to excessive wealth and influence in numerous countries, and are stridently unwilling to voluntarily return to face prosecution in the United Kingdom, collectively demonstrate a heightened risk of flight that no amount of bond could overcome,” the filing says.
The defense motion filed Friday acknowledges there is a presumption against bond in extradition proceedings but argues that release can be granted in special circumstances. It says the Tates’ high profile makes it nearly impossible for them to flee, and that they regularly post updates about their locations on social media.
While prosecutors call the brothers a flight risk, their attorneys said they have proved they are not by complying with all pretrial restrictions in Romania, where they are accused of luring women for sexual exploitation.
The UK has until mid-September to provide evidence to the State Department to support extradition, meaning the brothers could spend months in FDC Miami before the proceedings are resolved, the defense motion says. No date has been set for an extradition hearing. They are being held in a special unit for their own protection.
The brothers have long claimed that their violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes.
The former professional kickboxers, who have dual U.S. and U.K. citizenship, have millions of social media followers and are vocal supporters of President Donald Trump. The White House has said the brothers shouldn't expect any help from the president.
British prosecutors said the new charges relate to four new accusers and were brought after authorities received evidence from police in Bedfordshire, in southeastern England. The allegations, which span from 2010 to 2017, include rape, assault, trafficking and offenses relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.”
The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the U.K. between 2012 and 2015.
The brothers moved to Romania in 2016 and were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case hasn't moved forward due to legal and procedural problems.
The Tates' attorneys have said the Romanian court has granted a UK request for extradition that will take effect after Romanian proceedings conclude.
Andrew Tate, 39, became famous a decade ago when he was a contestant on the U.K. reality television show “Big Brother.” He was ejected from the show when a video appeared to show him assaulting a woman.
He has amassed over 10 million followers on X but has been banned from other platforms, including YouTube, TikTok and Instagram, for violating hate speech guidelines. He has made widely condemned comments, such as saying women who are sexually assaulted should bear some responsibility for the attacks and sharing graphic descriptions of how he might attack women.
Tristan Tate, 38, has worked with his brother on multiple businesses, including the production of online webcam pornography.

2026-08-11

16:34:53 KST

MOSCOW, August 11. /TASS/. The Russian Armed Forces carried out a coordinated overnight strike targeting defense industry facilities and transport and logistics centers in Kiev and Zaporozhye, the Defense Ministry reported.
TASS has compiled the main information about the attack’s aftermath.
Defense Ministry’s statement
- The Russian Armed Forces carried out a coordinated overnight strike using ground-based precision-guided weapons, resulting in the destruction of military-industrial facilities and transport and logistics centers in the cities of Kiev and Zaporozhye, the military said in a statement.
Facilities struck
- The ministry later revealed in another statement that the targets of the overnight strike were successfully hit.
- The Russian Armed Forces struck a Nova Post logistics terminal in Kiev, an automated compound storing and distributing dual-use goods, including components for long- and medium-range UAV production, robotic vehicles and electronic warfare systems.
- Russian servicemen also hit the Kiev-3 transport and logistics center, also known as San-park, a large warehouse facility of approximately 50,000 square meters that stored up to 15,000 attack FPV drones, including those equipped with thermal imaging cameras, such as Beshket, Spuk, Komik-A, and Gorobets, as well as ground control stations and related components.
- The Russian Armed Forces struck the Zaporozhstal steel mill (PJSC Zaporizhstal), a part of the Metinvest Group.
- It is a leading manufacturer of rolled sheet steel, which serves as the basis for creating protective structures, fortification modules, armor for military vehicles, and body armor plates.
- In addition, protective screens against FPV drone strikes were being installed on heavy armored vehicles on the plant’s premises.
Russian Aerospace Forces’ strikes
- The crews of the Russian Aerospace Forces delivered strikes against Ukrainian temporary deployment sites and drone control centers in the Donetsk People’s Republic, the Kharkov and Sumy Regions, the Defense Ministry noted.
- The strikes were carried out using FAB-250 aerial bombs equipped with a universal gliding and correction module and LMUR air-launched missiles.
- According to the ministry’s statement, Russian forces struck a temporary deployment site of Ukraine’s 63rd separate brigade near the settlement of Donetskoye in the DPR, a temporary deployment site of the 104th separate territorial defense brigade near the Boldyrevka settlement in the Kharkov Region, as well as a drone control center of the 119th separate territorial defense brigade in the Porozok settlement in the Sumy Region.
Situation in Ukraine
- The Kiev-controlled part of Zaporozhye is experiencing power outages due to earlier explosions, regional administration head Ivan Fyodorov reported on his Telegram channel.
- According to the official, several fires broke out in the city.
- A large fire engulfed Kiev warehouses after the explosions, the Ukrainian State Emergency Service said.
- According to its information, the fire was contained within an area of 1,200 square meters.
- Warehouses in the Kiev region were damaged, the regional administration reported on its Telegram.
- According to its information, the damaged warehouses were located in the Bucha district.

Russian wheat exports fall to lowest levels in almost ten years
Russian wheat exports in August could fall to their lowest in nearly a decade, agricultural analysts said on Tuesday, as the world's top wheat exporter contends with low prices and security risks on vital Black Sea shipping routes.
Russia and Ukraine have increasingly targeted ships and ports during their 4-1/2-year war, but both countries are harvesting large crops that could add to already ample global supplies.
The Sovecon agriculture consultancy said wheat exports could fall to an estimated 3-3.4 million metric tons versus 4.5 million tons a year ago, the lowest level since the 2016/17 season.
"Low export rates are increasing pressure on the domestic market," Sovecon head Andrey Sizov said.

Ukraine accuses Russia of systematic torture of detainees
Former Ukrainian detainees and Ukrainian officials accused Russia on Monday of systematically torturing prisoners of war and civilian detainees, holding captives incommunicado and subjecting them to beatings, electric shocks and sexual abuse, with thousands still in captivity.
Russia rejected the allegations made at an informal UN Security Council meeting, with its Deputy UN Representative Maria Zabolotskaya calling it "a disinformation campaign" and alleging that Russian prisoners in Ukraine were subjected to "torture and degradation and moral and physical abuse".
Khuan Alberto Levya Garsiya, still an active member of the Ukrainian military, said his Russian captors subjected him to every imaginable form of torture during 1,183 days in captivity.
Trump-Putin diplomacy fades as Russia-Ukraine war escalates
In the year since Donald Trump hosted Vladimir Putin on US soil for a summit designed to broker an end to Russia's offensive on Ukraine, the diplomatic initiative has fizzled out and the conflict has escalated.
For months, Russian officials talked up the "spirit of Anchorage" – a supposed climate of détente, renewed dialogue with Washington and a framework for finding a way out of the deadliest European conflict since World War II.
Now there are few traces of that atmosphere. US mediation efforts are at a standstill, both Russia and Ukraine are ramping up attacks and more civilians are being killed than at any point since the first months of the war.

Australia, Vietnam agree to deepen strategic, defense, economic ties
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:34:02 UTC
16:34:02 KST

Faisal Mahmud
11 August 2026•Update: 11 August 2026
Australia and Vietnam on Tuesday agreed to deepen their comprehensive strategic partnership across defense, security, trade, and clean energy during talks between Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Vietnamese President To Lam in Canberra.
The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a “peaceful, stable and prosperous Indo-Pacific” that is free from coercion and where sovereignty is respected, according to a statement from the Australian Prime Minister’s Office.
They expressed concern over developments in the South China Sea and stressed the importance of freedom of navigation and overflight, peaceful resolution of disputes, and adherence to international law, particularly the 1982 UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Albanese and Lam welcomed an updated joint vision for defense cooperation and agreed to expand collaboration in military training, maritime security, peacekeeping, search and rescue, information sharing, and counterterrorism.
The two countries will also strengthen cooperation against cybercrime, online scams, drug trafficking, human trafficking, and terrorism financing.
On economic ties, the leaders pledged to expand bilateral trade and investment, strengthen supply chains, and deepen cooperation in critical minerals.
They also welcomed agreements covering agriculture, vocational education, aviation, health, science, and technology.
Both sides committed to accelerating renewable energy deployment and strengthening cooperation on climate change, maintaining their goal of reaching net-zero emissions by 2050.
The leaders also called for an immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar, unhindered humanitarian access, and inclusive dialogue, while reaffirming support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture.

Hackers access Dutch credit card data in latest cyberattack
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Hackers access Dutch credit card data in latest cyberattack
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Simian, a Groningen-based company that owns a number of budget printing brands has warned customers in the Netherlands and Belgium that their personal details may have been stolen in a cyberattack.
In an email to affected customers, the company said attackers may have accessed email addresses and hashed passwords stored in its customer files.
Simian says on its website that it serves around 500,000 customers across its three brands Reclameland, Drukland and Flyerzone.
It has not said how many were affected by the breach, but that only a small number of customers had their credit card details intercepted. Those customers were contacted individually by phone and email, according to ANP.
Simian said it had reported the breach to the Dutch data protection authority AP and filed a report with police. It has brought in a specialist cybersecurity firm to investigate.
The company also said the leak did not originate in its own systems, but at an external service provider.
It confirmed the incident was not connected to the recent breach at CEVA Logistics, the delivery firm whose hack exposed customer data at Bol, De Bijenkorf, Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate.
The attack is the latest in a run of data breaches at Dutch companies, following the CEVA incident and, earlier this year, a mass hack at telecoms provider Odido.

Trump's secret flight out of Türkiye revealed after Iran threat
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:32:00 UTC
16:32:00 KST

President Donald Trump was secretly flown out of Türkiye aboard a military jet after U.S. officials determined that an Iranian threat against him was credible during last month's NATO summit, according to two senior U.S. officials familiar with the operation.
Trump and the public had been led to believe he left Türkiye on July 8 aboard an older version of Air Force One.
Instead, Trump was moved from that aircraft through a catering container and taken to a separate military plane that secretly flew him to Britain, one of the officials said.
The elaborate deception was designed to conceal Trump's whereabouts and prevent potential attackers from knowing which aircraft he was actually aboard.
Reporters traveling with Trump were not told about the switch.
They remained aboard the older Air Force One and flew to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in England, unknowingly serving as decoys while Trump traveled separately aboard a C-32A, a military version of the Boeing 757, according to the officials.
The Washington Post previously reported that the C-32A was the aircraft that carried Trump from Türkiye to Britain.
The operation was an unusual instance in which journalists assigned to cover a sitting president were deliberately misled about his location.
Trump had arrived in Türkiye aboard a luxury Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar. The aircraft is being considered for future use as Air Force One but has raised security concerns because it lacks some of the defensive capabilities found on the older presidential aircraft.
Trump publicly said he would leave Türkiye aboard the older Air Force One "for old time's sake."
At the airport, cameras captured Trump boarding the older aircraft through its usual left-side door. Journalists accompanying him boarded through the rear.
But Trump did not actually leave the country on that plane.
According to a U.S. official, a catering container was positioned on the opposite side of the aircraft, away from reporters. Trump was moved through the container and taken to the waiting military aircraft.
The reporters remained aboard the older Air Force One, unaware that the president was traveling separately.
The plane landed at Mildenhall at 10:16 p.m., according to a pool report. About 40 minutes later, Trump appeared, having already been secretly transferred back to the older Air Force One.
He then walked across the tarmac to the Qatari aircraft, where reporters were waiting. Trump and the press pool boarded the newer plane and flew to Washington.
The operation was assembled within hours after U.S. officials determined that a threat from Iran was credible, according to an official familiar with the planning.
Trump was briefed while in Türkiye, and a small group of senior officials was involved, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
The threat was not specifically tied to the Qatari aircraft. Officials said Trump was considered a target regardless of which plane he used.
The White House repeated a statement issued during the summit by communications director Steven Cheung, who said the administration used "distraction and misdirection" to counter threats against Trump.
The White House later reissued the statement without that phrase.
Former Secret Service agent Donald Mihalek said the agency has previously used decoy motorcades and flights to protect presidents, particularly in areas where there is a risk of combat.
During the flight back to Washington, reporters asked Trump why they had traveled to Britain aboard the older Air Force One.
Trump said he wanted troops at Mildenhall to see the newer Qatari aircraft. Asked why reporters had been instructed to keep their window shades closed during the flight from Türkiye, he said he knew of no specific threat but acknowledged Iran's longstanding hostility toward him.
"I'm number one on their list, before you," Trump told reporters. "But if I go, you go. Right?"
Trump has faced Iranian threats since ordering the 2020 killing of Gen. Qassim Suleimani during his first term. U.S. intelligence also warned during his 2024 campaign of potential Iranian plots against him, prompting increased security and occasional use of decoy aircraft.
The threats included an alleged murder-for-hire plot involving an Iranian proxy and the hacking of Trump campaign officials' accounts.
The secret flight came after reports raised questions about the security of the Qatari aircraft, angering Trump and prompting the Justice Department to subpoena journalists involved in reporting on the issue. Those subpoenas were later withdrawn after a federal judge criticized the process.

'A toxic brand': US support for Israel 'collapsing' among Democrats and Republicans, expert warns
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:31:54 UTC
16:31:54 KST

Israel is experiencing a deep erosion of support in the United States among both Democrats and Republicans, Prof. Yossi Shain, an expert on international relations, warned in an interview with 103FM on Monday.
Speaking about the changing attitude toward Israel in the American political arena, Shain, who formerly served as a Yisrael Beytenu MK, said that "Being anti-Israel in the US today is a hot commodity; it is worthwhile and rewarding, and not just anti-Israel, but anti-AIPAC."
"The entire idea around the world that Israel projects strength and that the Israeli lobby projects strength, and that it is not worth messing with it, is an idea that has collapsed in the US. Today, people are running for the Senate on hostility toward Israel, and that is what wins votes and victory," Shain argued.
Shain later addressed Israel’s relationship with the Democratic Party and the standing of the Jewish community in the United States. "We are in a long process of collapse," he explained. "David Hess, who headed the American Jewish Committee, recently said that US Jewry and Israel’s standing are like a building in Florida that collapsed on its residents.
"We can begin arguing about what causes what and how, but there is no doubt that two important points must be mentioned regarding Israel’s contribution. The State of Israel and the Israeli government simply betrayed the Democratic Party. Biden saved us, from their perspective, and we all went in the direction of Trump," he said.
US-Iran agreement will not happen, expert says
There will be no agreement between the US and Iran, Shain also stated.
"Israel would be praying for an agreement. At present, there will be no agreement, and future administrations will also not be bound by an agreement as they were in previous years, partly because of the issue of power. Therefore, there was no international political dialogue because we relied on Trump to do the work for us, after he pledged to 'pull the chestnuts out of the fire,'" he said.
Addressing the handling of Iran and the expectation that the United States would complete the process, Shain said that "The situation with Iran was that it had to be done within days. He asked us after we convinced him that we would bring down the regime and everything would collapse. Unfortunately, after our phenomenal victory with the Americans, we thought we would take another step forward, and America did not complete it."
"When America did not complete it, we kept chipping away more and more at its standing in the system and at its willingness," he noted. "On the Republican side, there is no willingness, from their perspective, for Israel to drag the US into another war," he said.
According to Shain, the erosion of support for Israel is no longer limited to the Democratic camp. "Unfortunately, Israel has become a toxic brand. This is no longer only a question of politics right now, although it is also connected to it. We have also become toxic among Republicans. People forget what this means, and it is not only with Tucker Carlson and others, you can see it spreading. I speak with the offices of senators who are supporters of Israel, and they are worried about this. The perception that Trump is not delivering is also filtering down to voters."
Israel 'genocide' campaign spreads to US education system
Shain also addressed the political considerations surrounding Trump and the changing attitudes among his supporters. "If in the past they said Trump wanted to reach the midterm elections, and therefore did not want to escalate because it did not win him points, right now there is concern that the lack of a decision is also costing him points among his supporters," he explained.
"On the one hand, there is the campaign that began immediately after the war in Gaza, about genocide, which has penetrated very deeply both intellectually and politically. On the other hand, it has penetrated to the point that even in the American education system, when you examine how the issue of genocide is taught, it is identified as an Israeli genocide," he added.
In conclusion, Shain warned of a continued deterioration in Israel’s standing in Washington. "If Israel does not replace its leadership with one perceived in America as sane, Israel does not have supporters even in the White House today," he said. "It is impossible to understand the scale of the fiasco. We are telling stories because we are in an election campaign, but this is something deep," he stated.

(서울=연합뉴스) 중국 동부를 강타한 제13호 태풍 '돌핀'으로 주택과 자동차 전시장이 물에 잠기는 등 피해가 속출했습니다. 건물 4층 창문에서 주꾸미가 발견되기까지 했습니다.
11일 로이터통신과 중국 현지 매체 등에 따르면 돌핀은 지난 9일 오후 5시 30분께 저장성 타이저우시 위환 부근에 최대풍속 초속 42ｍ의 위력으로 상륙했습니다.
로이터가 공개한 타이저우의 한 주택 영상에는 흙탕물이 가득 들어찬 집 안에서 어린이들이 물을 퍼내는 모습이 담겼습니다.
위환의 한 공장 4층에서는 작은 주꾸미 한 마리가 창문 바깥쪽에 붙어 있는 모습도 포착됐습니다. 다만 이 주꾸미가 어떻게 4층까지 올라왔는지는 확인되지 않았습니다.
돌핀이 몰고 온 비로 저장성 싼먼현에서는 누적 강수량이 970.3㎜에 달했고, 상하이 쉬자후이에는 40시간 연속 비가 내렸습니다. 상하이 공항 두 곳에서는 10일 하루 항공편 943편이 결항했습니다.
 자세한 내용은 풀영상으로 보시죠.

EU may delay new EES border checks for Brits to avert summer travel chaos

- EU Transport Commissioner Apostolos Tzitzikostas has reportedly given private assurances that biometric checks could be paused, following discussions with UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander.
- The new Entry/Exit System requires non-EU passengers entering or exiting the 29 Schengen countries to register biometric details, such as fingerprints and facial photos, replacing manual passport stamps.
- Operational unpreparedness at major European airports has led to widespread queue delays, prompting one in five British holidaymakers to consider cancelling their summer trips to Europe.
- To help mitigate potential travel disruption at British departure points, the UK government has announced £20 million in funding for additional passport check booths at the Port of Dover.

(서울=연합뉴스) 거대한 들소 한 마리가 남성을 공격합니다.
누운 자세로 움직이지 못하는 남성과 위협적으로 남성을 내려다보는 들소의 팽팽한 대치 상황이 이어집니다.
5일(현지시간) 폴란드 매체 TVP 등에 따르면 폴란드 비아워비에자 숲 근처에서 지난 3일 한 관광객이 야생 들소에게 지나치게 가깝게 접근하다 들소에 들이받히는 사고를 당했습니다.

영상 속 관광객은 종아리에 상처를 입은 것으로 알려졌습니다.
 지난달 초 미국 관광 명소인 옐로스톤 국립공원에서는 거대한 들소가 관광객을 들이받아 남성이 충격으로 2.4m 가까이 공중으로 튕겨 올랐다 바닥에 떨어지는 아찔한 사고도 발생했습니다.

 (로마=연합뉴스) 민경락 특파원 = 볼로디미르 젤렌스키 우크라이나 대통령이 11일(현지시간) 우크라이나가 북한산 탄도미사일을 동원한 러시아의 공격을 받았다고 주장했다.

New Forest fire ‘contained’ as firefighters begin third day of tackling ‘devastating’ blaze
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
08:26:42 BST
16:26:42 KST

Firefighter battling New Forest fire ‘for some time to come’ as emergency response enters third day
The A31 remains closed after National Highways confirmed the road surface suffered ‘significant’ damage
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
Firefighters are embarking on a third day of tackling a major blaze in the New Forest which officers report they are "managing to contain" after spending the night working "tirelessly".
Hampshire Fire and Rescue Service, aided by crews from neighbouring services, initially deployed 26 fire engines along with four water carriers to the A31 eastbound following 160 emergency calls regarding a van catching fire on Sunday evening.
The fire service confirmed that the flames spread from the burning vehicle onto the central reservation and then into nearby heathland, travelling south-easterly towards Backley Bottom within what is described as a "challenging rural location".
A Tuesday update from the fire service highlighted that a shift in wind direction had "provided a challenge" overnight, but crews managed to prevent further "spread and escalation" with aid from a police drone monitoring hotspots and flare-ups.
A total of seven fire engines, accompanied by water carriers and off-road vehicles, carried out the overnight response, continuously drawing water from a nearby lake through miles of laid piping using a high volume pump (HVP) system.
The A31 – the main arterial route across the New Forest – remains closed, with National Highways confirming that required repairs to "significant" damage affecting the road surface, safety barriers and boundary fencing can begin only once the fire is completely under control.
A deputy chief fire officer said firefighters are likely to be battling the New Forest fire “for some time to come”.
Shantha Dickinson, of Hampshire & Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service, said it had been a “very challenging few months so far for wildfires”, adding that tackling them was “incredibly resource-intensive”.
Discussing the New Forest fire, Ms Dickinson told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “Our firefighters and all of our emergency responders have been working in incredibly difficult conditions actually for the last 36 hours since the event started on Sunday evening due to a van fire.
“And we’re likely to be there for some time to come.”
She added: “We’re battling hard to get it under control.
“It currently covers an area of about a kilometre square. So just to put that into perspective, that’s about 140 football fields, so rolling heathland of beautiful countryside.”
The fire service said in a statement: “Crews have worked tirelessly throughout the night, a change in wind direction provided a challenge to the firefighting operations but thanks to the efforts of firefighters we are managing to contain the fire.
“We have been using a mix of fire engines and off-road vehicles to damp down and cool the edges of the area involved in the fire to prevent spread and escalation.
“The police drone is being used to enable us to prioritise hotspot areas and manage flare-ups.
“Overnight we had a slightly reduced presence with seven fire engines on site plus water carriers, off road vehicles and support vehicles but are planning to increase this for a larger scale attack today.
“We are maintaining water supply to the site through combination of water carriers and the High Volume Pump (HVP) system.
“We recognise that the hoses that have been laid as part of this system do in places go across access to homes in the area and we thank residents for their support and patience.
“The HVP allows us to move large amounts of water over a longer distance, helping crews maintain a continuous supply while they work to bring the fire under control.”
Gillie Molland, lead ranger for the New Forest National Park Authority, said that the affected area included protected lowland heathland which is home to “many nationally and internationally rare species – including all six of the UK’s reptiles, insects, plants and birds such as Dartford warblers and nightjar”.
She said: “Some rare heathland species may be lost or recover very slowly if local populations have been affected.”
Forestry England said it would be “carefully assessing the impact” of the fire after it was put out but said: “Incidents like this can be devastating to all of the things that make the New Forest so special.”
A Hampshire Constabulary spokeswoman said that 23 vehicles were left behind by motorists on Sunday, which were moved by police, with the owners asked to call 101 to be reunited with their vehicles.
Bournemouth Water, which supplies Ringwood and the New Forest, has asked residents to reduce water usage as the need for fighting the fire has added to the pressure put on supplies in the area because of the summer’s heatwaves.
General manager Richard Stanbrook said: “The prolonged hot weather over the last few weeks, paired with firefighting activity from recent large fires, has resulted in exceptionally high demand on our drinking water network.
“To help protect water supplies across the network and reduce the risk of supply interruptions, we are asking customers to reduce their water usage where possible until temperatures begin to drop.
“We all need to use water wisely in these extreme conditions, and small changes can make a big difference.”
Bournemouth Airport has advised customers to allow more time for their journeys while the A31 remains shut in both directions.

"레이시온·록히드마틴, 기술 이전 후 우크라 '성능개량'도 우려"
 
 (서울=연합뉴스) 곽민서 기자 = 미국이 우크라이나에 절실한 패트리엇 미사일 생산 면허를 내주겠다고 약속했다가 이를 사실상 번복한 것은 해당 기술이 러시아로 넘어갈 것을 우려했기 때문이라고 10일(현지시간) 영국 일간 텔레그래프가 보도했다.
 보도에 따르면 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령의 측근과 전문가들 사이에서는 최근 패트리엇 미사일이 우크라이나에서 생산될 경우 러시아가 관련 기술을 탈취할 수 있다는 우려가 제기됐다.
 우크라이나가 미사일을 자체 생산하려면 단순 부품이나 장비뿐 아니라 무기 조립용 설계도와 소프트웨어까지 현지로 이전해야 하는데, 이러한 기술이 전쟁 과정에서 러시아의 수중에 들어갈 경우 미국의 안보에도 중대한 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 것이다.
 패트리엇 미사일에는 비행 마지막 단계에서 적 미사일을 탐지해 요격미사일이 표적에 직접 충돌하도록 유도하는 첨단 장비인 'PAC-3 Ka 대역 능동 레이더 탐색기'가 탑재된다.
 미국은 이 같은 첨단 핵심 기술의 해외 이전을 엄격히 통제하고 있다.
 현재 20개국이 패트리엇 체계를 구매해 운용하고 있지만, 자체 생산 허가를 받은 나라는 독일과 일본뿐이다.
 아울러 패트리엇 미사일 개발에 참여한 레이시온과 록히드마틴 측에서 우크라이나가 패트리엇 생산 면허를 취득한 후 저렴한 비용으로 빠르게 생산할 수 있는 체계를 갖출 수도 있다는 의견이 나온 것으로 알려졌다.
 미 공화당의 한 관계자는 미국의 시사 잡지 디애틀랜틱에 백악관이 우크라이나에 허가를 거부한 또 다른 주요 이유는 이 때문이라고 전했다.
 우크라이나 측은 패트리엇 생산 기술 이전이 국가 존립과 직결된 문제라는 입장이다.
 우크라이나는 장기간 이어진 전쟁으로 요격미사일이 바닥나면서 방공망에 사실상 구멍이 뚫린 상태로 알려졌다.
 실제로 우크라이나는 지난 5일 러시아의 공습 당시 수도 키이우를 향해 발사된 탄도미사일 24발 가운데 단 한 발도 요격하지 못했다.
 우크라이나 정부와 군 수뇌부는 향후 방공망이 충분히 보강되지 않을 경우 이번 겨울 러시아의 공습이 재앙적인 결과로 이어질 수 있다고 우려하고 있다.
 볼로디미르 젤렌스키 우크라이나 대통령은 "요격미사일 시스템은 우리 국민의 생명을 구한다. 요격미사일 시스템이 부족한 매 순간 우리는 사상자를 내고 있다"고 호소했다고 텔레그래프는 전했다.
 앞서 트럼프 대통령은 지난달 30일(현지시간) 언론 인터뷰에서 우크라이나에 미사일 생산 면허를 내줄지 확실하지 않다는 입장을 밝혔다.
 이는 나토(NATO·북대서양조약기구) 정상회의에서 본인이 밝혔던 생산 면허 부여 방침에서 후퇴한 것이다.
 영국 일간 파이낸셜타임스(FT)에 따르면 트럼프 대통령은 당시 전화 인터뷰에서 "그것은 매우 비범한 무기이고, 우리는 누구에게 생산 면허를 내줄지에 대해 조금 신중해야 한다. 우리는 실상 (좀처럼) 장비 생산 면허를 내주지 않는다"고 말했다.
 mskwak@yna.co.kr

Israeli army blows up Palestinian man's home weeks after his killing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:25:11 UTC
16:25:11 KST

Qais Omar Darwesh and Lina Altawell
11 August 2026•Update: 11 August 2026
Less than three weeks after Palestinian man Farouk Ramadan was killed while confronting Israeli occupiers, the Israeli army blew up his house in the West Bank town of Tal.
Ramadan was among four Palestinians killed and four others injured during an attack by Israeli forces and occupiers on Tal in late July, according to local sources.
Ramadan, who was unarmed, seized a weapon from an occupier while confronting the attack on the village southwest of Nablus. He then opened fire on the occupiers and Israeli forces, killing two, according to the sources.
The Israeli army blew up the third floor of the residential building in Tal after raiding the area and forcing residents of several nearby homes to evacuate ahead of the demolition, Anadolu's correspondent reported.
Separately, the Israeli army began demolishing around 20 Palestinian shops and homes in the village of Anza, south of Jenin in the northern West Bank, allegedly for construction without permits, according to a local activist and Anadolu's correspondent.
Tayseer Sadaqa, an activist who documents Israeli violations in Anza, said the army raided the village with demolition vehicles and began tearing down around 20 shops located on the main road linking the village to Jenin.
“The demolitions are being carried out under the pretext of building without a permit,” Sadaqa told Anadolu.
The demolitions come amid an escalation in the destruction of Palestinian homes and other structures across the occupied West Bank, alongside illegal settlement expansion and the establishment of new outposts, according to Palestinian sources.
Since the start of Israel's genocide in Gaza on Oct. 8, 2023, Israeli forces and occupiers have escalated attacks in the West Bank, killing more than 1,183 Palestinians, injuring around 13,000 and arresting nearly 25,000, according to Palestinian figures.
Palestinians warn that the escalation is part of Israeli efforts to impose facts on the ground, paving the way for annexation of the occupied West Bank and undermining the possibility of establishing a Palestinian state along the 1967 borders under relevant UN resolutions.

Russian ballistic missiles struck the grounds of a Kyiv children’s hospital and set a warehouse ablaze — overnight strikes across Ukraine killed at least 9
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:25:03 UTC
16:25:03 KST

Russia struck the capital with ballistic missiles early on 11 August. One of them came down on the grounds of a Kyiv children's hospital in the Shevchenkivskyi district. Rescuers also fought a warehouse fire nearby that left one man injured.
The Kyiv children's hospital strike
Two craters opened on the hospital grounds, while the impact shattered windows and ruptured a gas line, rescuers reported. Utility crews sealed the leak within the hour. Staff at the Kyiv children's hospital had moved patients into the shelter before the strike, so it hurt no one there.
"Luckily, the children and medics were in the shelter — there were no casualties," - State Emergency Service reported
A warehouse ablaze and one man hurt
At a second address in the same district, a strike ignited a fire across 1,200 square meters of warehouse space. Crews first contained the flames, then put them out. Medics soon treated the lone casualty, a 28-year-old man. Earlier, the Air Force had warned of the ballistic threat before the missiles arrived.
Kyiv Oblast also under fire
The wider Kyiv Oblast took damage as well. In the Bucha district, the strike wrecked warehouse buildings and three trucks, although it caused no casualties. Officials said the enemy had again hit the region with ballistic missiles and attack drones.
A far deadlier night beyond Kyiv
Elsewhere, the toll climbed sharply. In Zaporizhzhia, a combined missile and guided-bomb strike killed six people and injured 19, regional authorities reported. Across the oblast, meanwhile, Russian forces launched 938 strikes on 58 settlements in a single day, injuring 52 residents in total. Officials also logged 341 reports of damage to homes, vehicles, and infrastructure.
In central Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, drones and artillery hit five districts more than 20 times. The strikes killed three people, among them a 15-year-old boy, and hurt five others, including a 7-year-old girl. To the northeast, an attack on Zlatopil in Kharkiv Oblast damaged civilian infrastructure and injured a resident.
Meanwhile, in Mykolaiv, drones hurt a 75-year-old woman and damaged homes and an industrial site, and officials described her condition as satisfactory. In nearby Snihurivka, six more drone strikes damaged houses, a shop, and a car, though they caused no injuries.
The strikes add to a wave of Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities this summer. The capital had already endured ballistic missiles days earlier, on the night of 8 August. That evening, explosions also echoed through Kyiv and Dnipro during a mass drone assault.

====================================================================================================

How do we prepare for climate change that's already here?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:25:00 UTC
16:25:00 KST

How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
August 11, 2026
In October 2023, the worst storm surge in more than 150 years hit the Baltic Sea coast. It destroyed dikes, collapsed coastal cliffs and devastated marinas in the northern German state of Schleswig-Holstein and parts of southern Denmark.
The catastrophic surge wiped away 2.68 meters (8.79 feet) of coastal bluff in Kiel, a port city and Schleswig-Holstein's capital. That was more than four times the yearly average lost over the previous two decades.
Human-caused climate change is supercharging extreme weather such as storms. And in coastal cities like Kiel, the consequences are already impossible to ignore.
"The impacts of climate change are hardly abstract in Kiel," said Martina Baum, who heads the city's climate adaptation division. "Since at least the 2023 storm surge, we have all been reminded of the profound effects it can have on us, on our daily lives, and on the environment around us."
Those effects are forcing Kiel — among the first cities to declare a climate emergency back in 2019 — to rethink its design, and how it works. It has since become a front-runner in adapting to the realities of a changing climate, establishing Baum's division in 2025 to help make the city more resilient to weather extremes and adopting an adaptation plan in February 2026 to step up those measures.
Is climate adaptation giving up on fighting climate change?
For city officials like Baum, adaptation is not a substitute for cutting the fossil fuel emissions heating the planet. Climate protection remains the first line of defense, because limiting warming will reduce future damage.
"For a long time, there was hesitation to engage officially with the issue of climate change adaptation. I also felt uneasy about it at first, because it felt as though it would somehow take the pressure off climate protection efforts," Baum told DW.
But the move to adaptation in Kiel reflects what's happening in other cities around the world from Santa Cruz in the US to Quezon City in the Philippines, as governments increasingly prepare for the impacts of heat, heavier rainfall and stronger storm surges that are already here.
That doesn't mean climate protection and adaptation always align. Installing power-hungry air-conditioning in housing, daycare or senior centers, for instance, protects vulnerable people in heat waves. But it increases energy consumption, "which would run counter to climate protection goals," Baum said.
"Even if we use renewable energy, demand is not yet covered by renewable sources 100% of the time, so any additional energy we consume will ultimately result in the emission of climate-damaging greenhouse gases," she added.
Redesigning cities for unavoidable impacts
While AC will sometimes be necessary, Kiel is working on solutions that cool the city naturally. It's adding vegetation to building facades, redesigning a park to channel cooler air into the city center, and making it easier for residents to access permits, information and grants for adaptation projects.
The city is also testing which tree species can survive future conditions. A decade ago, Kiel planted five specimens each of 20 different species to find out which can best withstand heat, drought and salt spray from the nearby Baltic Sea.
Trees provide shade, cool streets by roughly 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) and improve air quality, but not every species will thrive as the climate changes.
"There is no one-size-fits-all climate tree; different sites require different tree species," said Nicole Holz, who works in the department responsible for the city's green spaces.
The research requires patience.
"It's going to take some 20, 30 years until you get some real results," said Petra Holtappel, head of the same department.
Living differently: No more daytime soccer?
Adapting to climate change will also require changes to daily life, said Baum. Children, for example, may no longer be able to play soccer tournaments at 3 p.m. because it's too hot.
Although Kiel is getting warmer, it is expected to fare better than much hotter cities in Southern or Central Europe when it comes to heat. Still, the city is vulnerable to more storm surges and heavy rain and needs more retention areas to manage all that excess water. The city is dredging the park's pond to store stormwater during heavy rainfall, but is also exploring other ideas.
"One idea is what's known as multi-use design, meaning that in future, a soccer pitch could be built slightly lower than the surrounding area. During periods of heavy rain, water could then be directed there and allowed to gradually infiltrate into the ground or evaporate," Baum said.
The downside is the pitch might be unusable for up to 60 days a year, she added. But residents would need accept that, said Baum, who emphasized the need for greater public debate about adaptation measures.
How to reach people who don't think about the climate?
Helping residents understand those trade-offs and what's at stake is part of Annafried Stürmer's work. Stürmer organizes educational events, leads public excursions with scientists and attends neighborhood fairs to meet people who might not otherwise engage with climate issues.
At Kiel Week in June, the world's biggest annual sailing event, Stürmer displayed a map showing city flood risk from extreme rainfall.
"People often find that interesting, because it doesn't immediately seem like it's connected to climate change. Instead, the initial reaction is , 'Wow, if we get one of those intense heavy rainfall events, my house could be in serious trouble,' or 'My backyard could end up flooded,'" Stürmer said.
Stürmer has often found it easier to talk about climate adaptation than about climate change, because the former is more tangible.
"It's easier to talk about the need for a better-developed sewer system to handle heavy rainfall, or about planting different types of trees and vegetation, than it is to talk about reducing CO2 emissions," Stürmer told DW.
Recent record heat waves have made the adaptation conservation more urgent too.
"People noticed that it hadn't been as hot before," she said, adding residents increasingly recognize the need to protect children, the elderly, pregnant women and outdoor workers.
Climate adaptation not 'optional'
Even with growing public awareness of the need for adaptation, funding remains a problem in cash-strapped Kiel. Still seen as optional, climate action can quickly come under pressure when budgets tighten.
"I disagree with the idea that climate adaptation and climate action are optional responsibilities. I keep asking myself: what are the alternatives?" Baum said. "After all, it has been demonstrated time and again that investing in climate adaptation and climate mitigation will simply pay off."
Edited by: Jennifer Collins

Trump hid in catering cart during ‘surreal’ escape from Turkey
- President Donald Trump was secretly transferred off Air Force One onto a smaller military plane during his return from July’s Nato summit in Ankara, Turkey.

Congo says 2,000 people have died in its Ebola outbreak, the fastest growing on record
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
07:23:01 UTC
16:23:01 KST

Congo says 2,000 people have died in its Ebola outbreak, the fastest growing on record
BUNIA, Congo (AP) — At least 2,000 people have died in Congo’s Ebola outbreak, the fastest-growing on record, according to the latest data, as health authorities struggle to get help to remote localities due to rebel conflict, bad roads and work stoppages over payment issues.
Government data published overnight into Tuesday showed the outbreak has recorded a total of 4,381 confirmed cases, including 2,011 deaths. That death toll was reached almost three times faster than in the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak that was the worst in history.
The current outbreak was declared on May 15 but health authorities say sequencing showed it began months earlier, in February.
While it took about nine weeks for the outbreak to record the first 1,000 deaths, it’s taken just around three weeks for the figure to double, an evidence that the health crisis is moving faster than efforts to track and manage it.
The 2,000 death toll is “alarming” and calls for response efforts to double up in affected localities, said Dr. Jean-Marie Akandabo, who is helping manage patients at a local clinic in Ituri.
It’s already the second-largest outbreak in history, only behind the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that recorded more than 28,000 cases including over 11,000 deaths.
The Ebola outbreak is unlike most previous ones because the rare Bundibugyo virus responsible for it has no approved vaccines or treatments. Clinical trials for those have begun in Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, in eastern Congo.
Aid workers say the outbreak continues to outpace response that’s been expanding across the five eastern provinces affected. Many health workers have gone on strike to protest lack of payment for their work since the outbreak was declared. And WHO has said most new cases are still being recorded outside of contacts being monitored, showing that transmission remains out of the control of health workers.
This outbreak has killed a percentage of cases because of limited care
Ebola can be caused by different types of virus. Although the type responsible for the 2014-2016 outbreak is considered the deadliest, government data shows this Bundibugyo outbreak has killed a higher percentage of people as care and support are not getting to patients quickly enough. Many cases are reporting symptoms late or not at all.
The ongoing outbreak has so far had a case fatality rate of 45.9%, more than the 39.6% rate recorded in the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak.
“In the absence of an effective vaccine, control (for the outbreak) rests on identifying cases and then nursing them in secure facilities until they recover or sadly perish,” said Paul Hunter, a professor in medicine at the University of East Anglia in the U.K.
In a remote region like this with an ongoing conflict and interrupted communications, routine surveillance can be very difficult and “identifying cases early enough to prevent spread can be impossible,” said Hunter.
‘No one is safe’
Dr. Akandabo in Ituri said that the major challenges he’s seen is the limited care for patients and poor community engagement.
“We must not take this disease lightly, because it continues to kill and no one is safe.” said Akandabo.
The World Health Organization said on Monday that at the onset of the outbreak in one of Congo’s most remote and vulnerable areas, some cases were wrongly attributed to malaria and typhoid, and that early testing was conducted for the more common type of Ebola.
The WHO regional director for Africa, Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi, told a news conference that officials are “chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us.”
The first Ebola virus to be identified was in 1976 near the Ebola River in what is now Congo. The current outbreak is the 17th — and largest — the Central African nation has faced.
——
Asadu reported from Abuja, Nigeria

Lithuania’s Social Security and Labour Minister Inga Ruginienė has criticised a decision by the Vilnius city government to stop accepting written requests and complaints in Russian, saying the policy risks promoting social exclusion.
“The discussion about Russian-language proficiency is very strange,” Ruginienė told the radio Žinių Radijas on Tuesday.
Ruginienė said she supports the use of Lithuanian as the country’s official language but noted that some residents, particularly older people, still communicate primarily in Russian.
“To me, this is also a matter of respect,” she said. “Are we fostering exclusion and sorting people into good or bad, those with us or those against us? I do not particularly like this approach.”
The Vilnius municipality announced last week that it would no longer accept written applications and complaints from residents in Russian. Information in Russian and other non-European Union languages will only be provided orally only when a municipal employee is able to communicate in the requested language.
Russian has also been removed from the municipality’s website and administrative queue management systems.
Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius, a fellow social democrat, also questioned the decision, asking whether it was motivated by political considerations or intended as a communications stunt.
Vilnius Mayor Valdas Benkunskas defended the policy as part of the municipality’s “consistent approach” to language use.
At the same time, the municipality announced plans to expand Lithuanian-language learning opportunities for foreign residents.
More than 1,000 people are expected to take part in free Lithuanian-language courses and remote learning programs this year. The municipality has allocated an additional 300,000 euros for the initiative.

트럼프, 이란 암살 위협에 '위장 탈출'…에어포스원은 미끼였다
South Korea
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-11
16:19:24 KST
16:19:24 KST

지난달 나토 정상회의 후 에어포스원 탔다가 몰래 빠져나와 군용기 탑승 
에어포스원 탑승 취재진 '창문 덮개 내리라' 지시받아 전혀 눈치 못채
 
 (서울=연합뉴스) 김승욱 기자 = 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 지난달 북대서양조약기구(NATO·나토) 정상회의가 열린 튀르키예를 떠날 당시 이란의 암살 위협을 이유로 첩보 작전을 방불케 하는 '위장 탈출'을 감행한 사실이 뒤늦게 확인됐다.
 미국 일간 워싱턴포스트(WP)는 10일(현지시간) 트럼프 대통령이 지난달 8일 튀르키예 앙카라를 떠날 당시 백악관의 공식 발표와 달리 대통령 전용기(에어포스원)가 아닌 군용기인 C-32A에 숨어 탄 채 영국으로 향했다고 보도했다.
 당시 트럼프 대통령은 앙카라 공항에서 언론의 스포트라이트를 받으며 구형 에어포스원에 탑승했다.
 하지만 몇 분 뒤 트럼프 대통령과 일부 핵심 참모들은 기내 반대편 문으로 연결된 기내식 운반 트럭의 컨테이너에 몰래 올라탔다. 이 트럭에 달린 유압 실린더는 컨테이너를 여객기 출입문 높이까지 올렸다가 내리는 방식으로 작동한다.
 컨테이너를 통해 에어포스원에서 내린 트럼프 대통령은 곧바로 근처에 대기 중이던 C-32A로 옮겨탔다.
 이번 보도 이전까지 백악관 취재진은 트럼프 대통령이 자신들과 함께 에어포스원에 탑승한 채 영국으로 향한 것으로 알고 있었다. 에어포스원에 탑승해 있던 취재진은 당시 상황을 눈치채지 못하도록 창문 덮개를 내리라는 지시를 받았다고 한다.
 결국 취재진과 백악관 직원들이 타고 있던 에어포스원은 이란으로부터 트럼프 대통령이 공격당할 가능성을 분산시키기 위한 '미끼' 역할을 수행했다고 WP는 전했다.
 트럼프 대통령이 탑승한 C-32A 수송기는 추적 시스템을 끈 채 미국 대통령이 탑승한 항공기에 부여되는 항공교통 관제용 호출부호인 '에어포스원'이 아닌 '리치 18'이라는 평범한 호출부호를 사용하면서 영국 밀든홀 공군기지로 비행했다.
 영국에 도착한 트럼프 대통령은 취재진이 눈치채지 못하게끔 황급히 에어포스원으로 옮겨 탄 뒤 카메라 앞에 나타나 미군 장병들을 격려했다.
 이후 그는 카타르로부터 기증받아 정비한 신형 에어포스원으로 바꿔타고 미국으로 귀국했다.
 당시에는 트럼프 대통령이 이란의 암살 위협이 있다는 판단 아래 튀르키예에서 구형 에어포스원을 타고 영국으로 간 뒤 그곳에서 신형 에어포스원으로 갈아탄 것으로만 알려졌다.
 이렇게 알려졌던 것에서 더 나아가 트럼프 대통령이 군용기를 몰래 갈아탄 채 튀르키예에서 영국까지 비행하는 극단적인 기만 작전을 벌인 것은 이란의 구체적인 암살 위협이 있었기 때문이라고 WP는 전했다.
 트럼프 대통령은 새 에어포스원에서 약 15분간 기자들과 대화를 나누면서 이란의 암살 위협을 강조했지만, 앞서 있었던 기만 작전에 대해서는 전혀 언급하지 않았다.
 그는 튀르키예 공항에서 기자들에게 기내 창문 덮개를 내리라는 지시가 내려졌던 것과 관련해서는 "우리가 상대해야 하는 그 더러운 인간들 때문에 위험한 비행을 하고 있었기 때문"이라고 답했다.
